課名: 生物資訊於微生物學之應用
開課系所: 農業化學系 / 農業化學研究所
課程概述: 本課程為生物資訊學核心概念的實作導論。生物資訊學是結合生物學、電腦科學與統計數據分析的一門學科。學生將親自分析來自高通量定序的核酸序列。
課程目標:
1. 理解生物資訊學的核心概念與應用 
學生能夠解釋生物資訊學的基本原理，並了解其在微生物學研究中的實際應用，特別是在微生物群落結構分析方面。
2. 建立生物資訊學工作環境與操作技能 
學生能夠安裝相關軟體工具，並能以UNIX命令行以進行生物數據處理與分析。

課名: 農產與食品質譜學概論
開課系所: 農業化學系 / 農業化學研究所
課程概述:
本課程為學士班高年級與研究所學生所設計，旨在協助學生建立質譜分析的基礎概念，並探索其在農產品與食品科學、加工研究及化學性食品安全評估中的應用。課程內容涵蓋質譜分析的核心組成，包括樣品前處理、基本層析分離原理、常用離子化技術、質量分析器運作、資料解析與圖譜判讀、定量策略與方法驗證。課程同時強調質譜於農產品化學成分分析、食品品質與功能成分研究、食品加工反應追蹤、污染物偵測以及法規監管實務中的多元應用。
本課程的核心目標是使學生能掌握質譜的基本原理、理解研究文獻中的質譜技術內容，並能根據研究問題選擇合適的質譜平台與分析策略，以應用於農產品品質研究、食品化學探討與食品安全分析。
課程目標:
I.	基礎原理理解：理解質譜分析的基本原理、常用離子化技術與質量分析器之運作方式，並說明質譜在農產品與食品科學中的應用角色。
II.	文獻判讀與方法學掌握：理解質譜分析方法學，包括樣品前處理、層析、離子化、質量分析與 MS/MS 解譯，並能判讀研究文獻中的相關質譜分析結果。
III.	技術選擇與分析規劃：能依據研究問題或實務需求，選擇適當的質譜平台（如 LC-MS、GC-MS、HRMS）與分析策略，作為農產品品質評估、食品化學研究或食品安全檢測方法設計之基礎。
課程要求:
1.	先修科目：普通化學；並建議曾修習分析化學或食品分析
2.	課後研讀相關文獻並參與課堂討論。

課程概述:
This course will be taught in English.
Topics include:
The consolidation process, including changes in ownership interests
Indirect and mutual holdings
Subsidiary preferred stock
Consolidated earnings per share
Derivatives and foreign currency transactions
This course builds on the knowledge from previous financial accounting classes, especially Intermediate Financial Accounting.
課程目標:
This course aims to develop key accounting competencies, focusing on the following learning goals:
1. Accurately calculate the amounts for consolidated financial statements, including adjustments for changes in ownership interests
2. Analyze the impact of indirect and mutual holdings on consolidated financial statements.
3. Calculate and prepare adjustment entries for the elimination of indirect and mutual holdings.
4. Adjust the allocation of net income between common and preferred shareholders in group enterprises.
5. Compute consolidated EPS for group enterprises, including adjustments for diluted EPS scenarios.
6. Analyze and account for the use of derivatives for hedging purposes in group enterprises.
7. Record and adjust for the fair value changes of derivatives in the context of consolidated financial statements.
8. Account for foreign currency transactions, including translation of foreign operations.

課程概述: This course builds on students’ prior knowledge of audit planning and focuses on how financial statement audits are carried out in practice. The course examines how auditors identify and respond to fraud risk, understand information technology (IT) controls, apply audit sampling, and gather audit evidence to support audit conclusions. Students will also learn how audits are completed and how audit results are communicated through the auditor’s report.
課程目標:
A major component of the course is the application of audit procedures to key financial statement cycles, including sales and collections, acquisitions and payments, inventory and warehousing, cash and financial instruments, and financing activities. Through lectures, examples, and practice problems, students will learn how auditors connect risks, internal controls, audit procedures, and audit evidence. By the end of the course, students should have a clear understanding of how audit work is performed and how audit evidence supports the final audit opinion.

In this semester, the primary learning objectives are to:
1. Understand and evaluate the responsibilities and objectives of external auditors
Students will understand the objectives of financial statement audits and the responsibilities of external auditors, including the use of professional judgment and professional skepticism. Students will also learn how auditors address fraud risk and how IT controls affect audit procedures.

2. Apply audit procedures related and requirements to audit sampling, audit completion, and the auditor’s report
Students will be able to apply basic audit sampling concepts, evaluate audit evidence, and understand how sampling results affect audit conclusions. Students will also learn key audit completion activities, such as evaluating misstatements, reviewing subsequent events, and understanding going concern issues, as well as how different auditor’s reports communicate audit results to users.

3. Perform audit procedures for major financial statement cycles
Students will be able to perform and evaluate audit procedures for major financial statement cycles, including revenue, expenditures, inventory, cash, and financing. This includes understanding of detailed tests of controls, appropriate substantive procedures, and evaluating whether audit evidence supports audit conclusions.

課程概述:
This course is to discuss special topics on intermediate accounting, including revenue recognition, leasing, tax accounting, pension, preparation of statement of cash flows, and accounting errors and changes.

The course will be jointly instructed by Yu-Fang Chu and Hsin-Tsai Liu. Yu-Fang Chu will cover the topics scheduled before the midterm exam. Hsin-Tsai Liu will teach the topics in the second half of the semester. The final exam will focus primarily on the materials covered after the midterm. Students should pay attention to the course schedule to keep track of the transition between instructors and course topics.
課程目標:
1. Revenue Recognition
After completing this topic, students will be able to explain the core principle of revenue recognition and apply the revenue recognition model to contracts with customers. Students will understand how to identify performance obligations, and recognize revenue when (or as) performance obligations are satisfied. Emphasis is placed on analyzing contracts, exercising professional judgment, and understanding how estimates and variable consideration affect the timing and amount of revenue recognized. 

2. Leasing
After completing this topic, students will be able to identify lease arrangements and explain the accounting for leases from the lessee’s perspective. Students will understand how to recognize and measure right-of-use assets and lease liabilities and how lease transactions affect the financial statements. Emphasis is placed on determining lease terms, discount rates, and lease payments, as well as accounting for lease modifications and reassessments.

3. Income Tax Accounting
After completing this topic, students will be able to explain the objectives of income tax accounting and distinguish between accounting income and taxable income. Students will understand temporary and permanent differences and how these differences result in deferred tax assets and liabilities. Emphasis is placed on measuring income tax expense, accounting for net operating loss carryforwards, and assessing the need for valuation allowances. 

4. Pension and Other Post-Employment Benefits
After completing this topic, students will be able to explain the accounting for defined benefit pension plans and identify the components of pension expense. Students will understand how pension obligations and plan assets are measured and how actuarial assumptions affect reported amounts. Emphasis is placed on the recognition and presentation of pension-related items in the financial statements and other comprehensive income. 

5. Statement of Cash Flows
After completing this topic, students will be able to explain the purpose and content of the statement of cash flows. Students will understand how cash flows are classified into operating, investing, and financing activities and how the statement of cash flows complements accrual-based financial statements. Emphasis is placed on preparing the statement of cash flows using the indirect method and understanding common classification issues. 

6. Accounting Errors and Changes
After completing this topic, students will be able to distinguish between accounting errors, changes in accounting principles, and changes in accounting estimates. Students will understand the appropriate accounting treatment for each type of change, including retrospective and prospective application.

課程目標:
Every asset (liability) has a value. We just have to find it. The objective of this course is to teach students how to use accounting (financial) information in valuation and, particularly, how to obtain fair value estimates for financial reporting purposes. 
This course aims to provide students with the knowledge they need to obtain estimates of the fair value either of single financial (possibly nonfinancial) assets and whole firms using intrinsic and relative valuation approaches. Contingent valuation will also be covered in this course. The course covers the mechanics of the accounting process; the foundation for financial reporting; the differences and similarities in income statements, balance sheets, and cash flow statements around the world; examines the implications for securities valuation of any financial statement element or transaction, and shows how different financial statement analysis techniques can provide valuable clues into a company's operations and risk characteristics. In a nutshell, the course starts from business and accounting analysis, followed by financial analysis, and concludes with the discussion of theories of valuation.

課程目的：

由PwC具有豐富併購經驗之財務、稅務、法律、會計及人資專家，從實務的角度講授與企業併購有關之各種面向與課題，課程重點包括：

1. 併購總覽：介紹企業併購的流程與週期，說明併購如何協助企業成長、轉型與提升競爭力，並探討產業趨勢與策略思維。
2. 盡職調查：解析財務、法律、稅務等多面向的盡職調查重點，協助買方辨識風險、確認交易合理性，為後續談判與整合奠定基礎。
3. 價值評估：介紹資產法、市場法、收益法等常見評價方法，說明如何衡量企業價值並進行價格談判，掌握併購交易的核心。
4. 併購會計：說明併購會計的基本概念、收購法、商譽與價格分攤（PPA），並探討會計在併購決策與財報呈現上的關鍵角色。
5. 併購稅務：探討併購過程中常見的稅務議題，包括交易架構、稅務盡職調查、商譽攤銷與租稅優惠，協助企業規劃最適稅務策略。
6. 併購法律：解析併購相關法律規範、併購契約、公司治理與法規遵循，強調法律在風險控管與交易安全中的重要性。
7. 資料分析與AI應用：介紹資料分析與AI在併購流程中的應用
8. 專題演講：邀請產業專家分享併購策略及產業面洞見。
9. 分組案例研究：透過分組討論實際併購案例，強化分析、解決問題與團隊合作能力，提升對併購實務的理解與應用。

課程概述:
This course bridges the gap between general language acquisition and the specialized communication skills required for academic success, professional development, and global citizenship.

The Integrated Science & Technology (綜合科技) track: Tailored for the digital age, this track focuses on reading, listening, and presentation skills within tech-driven contexts. Students learn to communicate effectively in English using modern technology, preparing them for the academic and professional demands of the 21st-century workplace.
課程目標:
The primary goal of this track is to transform students from "English learners" into "Technical Communicators" who can navigate the digital and scientific landscape with precision.

1. Mastering Technical Literacy
Students will move beyond general vocabulary to master the language of innovation.

Goal: Read and listen to complex technical content (e.g., AI ethics, biotech breakthroughs, or climate data) and extract key information.

Action: Use Concept Mapping to organize complex scientific data into clear, logical structures.

2. Digital Communication and Presentation
In the modern workplace, how you deliver information is as important as the information itself.

Goal: Deliver persuasive technical presentations that simplify complex data for diverse audiences.

Action: Apply Monroe's Motivated Sequence to structure tech pitches or research findings in a way that captures attention and inspires action.

3. Critical Evaluation of Technology
Students will not just use technology, but critique its impact on society.

Goal: Analyze the ethical implications of 21st-century advancements (e.g., data privacy or automation).

Action: Transition from surface-level understanding to Critical Synthesis, comparing different expert viewpoints to form an independent conclusion.

Active participation and in-class performance (including quizzes and tasks): 40%

Written exams: 60%

1.	學會開口說印尼語！增加台灣學生對世界第五大語言，有3億語言人口東南亞語言之一的印尼語，以及相關族群文化的認識與了解。
2.	培養台灣學生印尼語日常會話和基本閱讀的基礎能力。
3.	培養台灣學生關注與關懷在台印尼人士、社區與議題。
評量方式:
本校尚無訂定 A+ 比例上限。
本校採用等第制評定成績，學生成績評量辦法中的百分制分數區間與單科成績對照表僅供參考，授課教師可依等第定義調整分數區間。詳見 學習評量專區。
備註: 第一週未請假缺席則視同退選。第二週後不開放加選。母語人士(包括馬來西亞籍)勿修習。不開放旁聽。

課程概述:
印尼語在台灣的需求越來越高，除了在台灣約有三十萬人的印尼移工、外配、外配第二代之外，印尼有兩億五千萬人口，為東協最具發展性的國家，就業與投資市場越來越大，對印尼語和中文雙語能力的需求，也越來越多。本課程將是全台灣的大學中，唯一開辦的印尼語教學課程的第三、四個學期（即第二學年的進階課程），主要為台灣學生奠定印尼語基礎與進階能力，培育印尼語專才。
　　本課程跳脫傳統語言學習的方式，除了傳統課程講授之外，主力放在語言、文化與生活體驗的結合。讓學生在掌握了基礎印尼語字彙和句型之後，能夠更自在使用語言。此外，也讓學習語言變成一種主動式的學習活動，成為學生未來在語言上推進的動力。本課程強調實作活動，即由學生經由分組和個人作業的方式，實際練習、操作，把語言學習作為一種行動式的學習策略，從應用、參與到設計，將語言學習融入學生的專業中。
　　印尼文二的課程內容，上下學期各分成三大部份。上學期第一部份，規劃不同情境，讓學生練習口說和聽力能力。第二部份，著重用印尼文發音的動畫或慢畫上，讓學生學習生動的生活化口語。第三部份，則是實作的部份，請學生跟據一張圖片，或自行繪畫，創作一篇簡短的故事，並用印尼文來書寫。

教學方式：
1. 透過教師講授、影音教材等來訓練語言的聆聽、說話、閱讀、理解和寫作的能力。
2. 透過印尼語的學習，相關文化知識與市場分析，了解東南亞、印尼的文化與生活經驗。
3. 設計參與式的期末報告，引導同學們利用印尼語來介紹台灣，更進一步成為傳遞多元文化的角色。
課程目標:
1. 增加學生對印尼語的應用，讓學生掌握印尼文的動詞、名詞變化，準備學生面對未來的印尼就業市場。
2. 增加印尼語課的實用性與趣味性，以傳統講授、圖文和影音的方式展現對語言的掌握。
3.透過語言學習與實作課程，增進台灣學生對印尼文化與社會的認識與了解。
4. 培養學生印尼語的口說、聆聽、進階閱讀與寫作的能力。
5. 透過語言與文化的學習與實作，讓印尼人更了解台灣文化，進而推廣台灣。
課程要求:
1. 本課程的報告為小組報告結合個人報告的方式，以書面報告或簡報方式呈現，讓台灣人更了解印尼文化與語言。
2. 請學生進行印尼文作品創作，形式不拘，例如圖文並茂、繪本等形式。

課程概述: 本課程的教學目標，將以「基礎韓語」為主，教授基本生活用語，例如：問候語、家人朋友之稱呼、飲食、交通、季節、天氣，以及休閒活動……等。除此之外，在課程安排方面，將透過師生之間的互動與討論，讓學生更能體驗多樣化的韓國文化。
課程目標:
一、	基礎韓語：
（一）	韓語發音：進一步介紹韓語發音規則。
（二）	基礎韓語會話：練習慣用會語、背好單字及其運用。
二、	韓語會話：盡量讓同學上課時「多發音、多練習、多應用」之原則。除教材之單字外，適時提供補充教材，以增進學生學習效果。
三、	韓國及韓國文化：各種韓流文化在臺灣廣受歡迎，透過媒體認識韓國及韓國文化的頗多，而有時因資訊不全或錯誤印象導致彼此之間的誤解。本課程除教材教學外，關心韓國動態進行討論，讓學生進一步認識韓國。

課程概述:
在東南亞地區，泰國自古以來是個重要的營運中心之國。在觀光方面，目前泰國已經是東南亞最受歡迎的國家；在經濟方面，泰國已經是新興市場中值得投資的一個重要目標之一，每一年有不少的台灣人到泰國去旅遊與投資設工廠，甚至到泰國去工作、退休後定居。同時也有很多泰國人到台灣來工作與觀光，根據駐台灣泰國經濟文化辦事處（勞工局）的統計，在台灣的泰國勞工曾經高達十二萬人。
因此，我們不能否認泰國與台灣往來的重要與衝擊，我們應該更進一步去了解泰國與東南亞國家之間的各方面，如：文化、思想、歷史、政治、經濟，以及最不可或缺的就是「語言」，因為「語言」是我們能了解其他文化之「鑰匙」，若我們沒有這把「鑰匙」我們更不能談得上文化。
課程目標:
1.能了解曼谷話，曼谷話是泰語的標準國語。
2.在短期內能聽、說、讀、寫常用泰語、自我介紹、打招呼、問路、買東西等基本技能之觀光與生活會話。
3.在文化方面，認識泰國的觀光勝地,泰國人的思想、文化、風俗習慣、泰國節日（如：波水節、水登節、守夏節、解夏節、禮佛節等）、泰國人的基本禮貌（如：合掌、說話、送禮、禁忌）、泰國人的門族性（如：溫和好客、從來不排華或訪客、沒有種族歧視）。
4.在歷史方面，認識泰國的近代史，如：素可泰王朝、阿域他雅王朝、吞武力王朝、曼谷王朝之簡介。
5.在文法方面，認識泰語的基礎語法，如：泰語的句子結構（ＳＶＯ）、泰語的現在式、進形式、未來式、基本的詞彙、量詞、數字等。
6.在語音方面，能習得泰語的語音學，如：44個子音、32個母音、5個聲調。
7.在文字方面，能認識泰文的字母、韻母、調號，並能正確地熟悉與熟練泰文文字。
8.此班採取本人編著的為教材，另有練習作業簿，若有課外的補充資料將會於日後補發。

In addition, students are also expected to practice their oral skills outside of class, such as by engaging in conversations with (native) English speakers. Students are also expected to complete all assignments on time. Finally, students should be open to feedback and constructive criticism from the instructor and their peers in order to continue to develop their oral communication skills.

課程概述: This course analyzes agriculture’s pivotal role as an engine of economic growth and structural transformation. Students will master microeconomic tools—including social welfare analysis and production theory—to evaluate how trade, price policy, and market power shape global welfare. We compare regional development paths across Asia, Africa, and Latin America to understand how resource scarcities induce technological and institutional innovation. The curriculum further explores the human dimensions of development, investigating the economics of poverty traps, the nutrition transition, and rural-urban migration. We conclude by addressing 21st-century risks, specifically climate resilience and the political economy of agricultural research.

5. Assess Future Resilience in Global Food Systems

課名: 環境與自然資源經濟學
開課系所: 農業經濟學系 / 生物多樣性學分學程
課程概述:
Once a (sub)field almost exclusively studied by agricultural economists, environmental and natural resource economics has emerged as the arguably most dynamic field in economics, experiencing unprecedented growth due to the relaxed budget constraints and changed utility functions of modern citizens.

The course navigates the current landscape of environmental and natural resource economics, in which the concepts of externality and equality are more important than ever. While offering a global perspective potentially biased by thoughts from developed countries, the course is committed to provide a more balanced local view for future leaders in Taiwan, an economically developed yet environmentally developing country.

The first part of the course will delve into the fundamental concepts and theories of environmental and natural resource economics and introduce the empirical methods for valuing environmental and nonmarket goods. In the second part of the course, we will look at the causes and consequences of environmental pollution. We will then dedicate a significant amount of our time to the issue of climate change, arguably the biggest threat to the continuation of human civilization, including its consequences and potential (and sometimes dubious) solutions from an empirical perspective. By involving a significant component of intertemporal considerations, we we will cultivate a sense of responsibility to actively contribute to safeguarding our future generations, despite knowing that we are not the (primary) culprits of current environmental crises.

Disclaimer: the instructor is notorious for being "careless" of grades. This course is very likely a bad option for students who care only about GPAs.

* To ensure timely responses from the instructor, please send all course-related inquiries using your NTU email.
課程目標: By the conclusion of this course, students will gain an appreciation for the essential role of environmental and natural resource economics in shaping our world and (hopefully better) future. Many will also realize that this field is far more relevant than they previously imagined or perceived and that economics, although being anthropocentric, is not only about human. In some cases, students might start to recognize environmental and natural resource economics being the most indispensable part of economics: people may choose not to interact with any fellow humans, but they can certainly not live by detaching themselves from the natural environment.

Midterm project

Students are asked to complete a research proposal, due 04/19, for valuing some environmental (dis)amenities. The proposal should at least 1) clearly define the good to be valued, 2) describe the research area and valuation method, and 3) outline the empirical research design. A research design may include, for example, data source and collection method, empirical models, hypotheses or expected findings, and survey instrument. A complete research report, i.e., with results, are encouraged but not expected. 開課系所: 農業經濟學系 / 農業經濟學研究所
課程概述:
碳定價是國際上因應氣候變遷的主要因應措施之一；其基本精神為排碳有價的落實、透過各種不同的碳定價方法，將溫室氣體排放對於環境所造成的各種成本與排放行為的受益者進行關聯，進而藉此減少排放。經過各國實務應用的開展，目前已可歸納出四種常見的碳定價方法，分別是排放交易、碳環境稅費、碳信用機制以及內部碳定價，各具備不同的設計特徵及操作內涵。在本課程中，重點即在於針對前述碳定價工具進行介紹.。

Carbon pricing is one of the main response measures to address climate change. Through various carbon pricing methods, the costs of greenhouse gas emissions on the environment are linked to the beneficiaries of the emissions, thereby reducing emissions. From the practical applications in different countries, four common carbon pricing methods have been summarized: Emission Trading Scheme, Carbon Tax, Carbon Crediting Mechanism, and Internal Carbon Pricing, each with distinct design features and operational implications. This course focuses on introducing the aforementioned carbon pricing tools.
課程目標:
本課程之主要目的，即在於結合理論及實務，一方面增進選課同學對於碳定價內涵的理解，另一方面則期待培養碳定價工具實務應用之設計能力。

The main objective of this course is to integrate theory and practice to enhance students' understanding of the principles of carbon pricing while also developing their ability to design practical applications of carbon pricing tools.

1. 背景脈絡：國內外氣候治理概況與產業碳風險
2. 碳定價工具：總量管理排放交易機制 (cap and trade)
3. 碳定價工具：碳環境稅費 (carbon tax/levy)
4. 碳定價工具：碳信用抵換機制 (carbon crediting mechanism)
5. 碳定價工具：內部碳定價 (internal carbon pricing)
6. 碳管理實務：碳盤查 (inventory), 碳足跡 (carbon footprint), 碳中和 (carbon neutrality)

課程概述:
A.何謂 AGE or CGE  模型？
本課程是介紹分析工具，此模型是研究總體經濟問題的利器。 AGE 的基本思想是在總個經濟中，由於供給和需求是互關聯的，使得部門或市場的變化會傳遞到其他部門和市。
AGE 模型由一系列描述不同經濟部門、市場和要素之間關係的方程式構成，用以分析各種經濟政策和外部衝擊 (如稅收、貿易、環境、政治) 的影響。我們可以採用模擬分析來評估它們對經濟體系中關鍵指標的影響，如就業、產出、通膨、收入分配等。

B.如何學好 AGE or CGE  模型？
要有效掌握並合理運用 CGE 模型，需要理解兩個要點：
1. 可計算的 (Computable)： 為了保證我們的模型不是空中樓閣，該模型通常會與投入產出表資料結合，使其比其他 GE 模型更接近真實。
2. 一般均衡(General Equilibrium)： 相對於個體經濟學中的部分均衡，一般均衡考慮了整個社會體系的最優決策，考慮了直接效應和間接效應，因此模型模擬的結果也更客觀。

C. AGE or CGE  模型用在何處？
AGE or CGE  模型在經濟學研究和政策分析上有廣泛的應用，尤其是針對那些較為複雜的總體經濟問題和政策影響。例如：
1.貿易政策分析： 關稅變動、貿易自由化與貿易協定的實施。透過這種模型，研究人員可以分析各個產業和區域在貿易政策變化下的生產、就業和收入變化。
2.稅收政策分析： 所得稅、消費稅、企業稅等。這有助於了解稅收政策變化對資源分配、生產和消費的影響。
3.環境政策分析： 碳排放稅、排放配額制度等。透過模擬這些政策，可以評估它們對產業結構、能源使用和環境品質的影響。
4.發展政策評估： 貧窮減緩政策、基礎建設等。這有助於了解這些政策對不同社會群體和經濟部門的響。
課程目標:

課程概述:
本年度計量經濟學專論主題為因果推論與機器學習

This course is a required course for doctoral students and is also suitable for master's students who wish to pursue empirical research in economics and related fields. The objective of this course is to equip students with a comprehensive set of statistical tools and research designs that are pivotal for producing high-quality research in applied microeconomics. The course places a strong emphasis on methods for estimating causal effects and understanding their applications.

Unlike many other econometrics courses aimed at future econometricians, this course is tailored for applied practitioners. It prioritizes research design over statistical technique and focuses on real-world applications rather than theoretical proofs. The curriculum covers an array of cutting-edge empirical methods for causal inference and machine learning, including matching methods, difference-in-differences design, synthetic control, regression discontinuity design, instrumental variables, as well as machine learning techniques such as LASSO, random forests, and causal forests for estimating heterogeneous treatment effects. In addition, the course introduces students to working with geospatial data (GIS) and other emerging data sources beyond standard survey data.

Throughout the course, we place a strong emphasis on the practical implementation of these methods and on best practices in managing real-world data. Students will apply what they learn by writing a term paper, which must be typeset using LaTeX. By the end of the course, students should have built a solid foundation for conducting independent empirical research and for writing future master’s and doctoral theses.

五、課程簡介： 
主要目的：認識台灣的森林、林學實習包括之領域。由森林生態系的組成、構造，其間之相互關係了解森林的演替過程。體會大自然的奧妙及維護一片健康森林的重要及心血。進一步由介紹森林涵養水源、淨化空氣、景觀遊憩、森林保健（森林浴）、水土保持（治山防洪─集水區經營）等將自有人類以來,與人類生存、文明息息相關的”森林”讓同學們有機會親身體驗。 
主要內容如下： 
1.	人工林之介紹及調查 
2.	天然林之調查、分析 
3.	造床、播種、扞插 
4.	除草、修枝、間伐 
5.	拜訪森林─森林浴之體驗 
6.	921地震之震撼─認識震後之山林 
7.	自然保護區之介紹、調查 
8.	森林療育

課程概述:
This introductory statistics course provides students in biology, agriculture, and related life sciences with essential statistical foundations for understanding and conducting research. Statistics is crucial in modern biology, from analyzing experimental results and comparing treatment effects to evaluating field trials and making sense of complex biological data, making statistical literacy essential for success in the life sciences.

The course connects theoretical statistics with practical applications directly relevant to biological and agricultural research contexts, with strong emphasis on applied problem solving rather than mathematical theory. Students will work with datasets from ecology, genetics, plant science, animal science, and agricultural field trials, gaining experience with the types of data and research questions they will encounter in their studies and research. Lecture sessions introduce statistical concepts and methods, while laboratory sessions provide hands-on practice. Students will develop skill sets to interpret and explain data through visualization, exploratory data analysis, statistical inference, and the use of R, an open source software widely used in biological data science.

Topics covered include:  descriptive statistics and modern data visualization techniques, probability theory and probability distributions (both discrete and continuous), sampling methods and the Central Limit Theorem, point estimation and interval estimation, hypothesis testing frameworks and p values, one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) for experimental data, correlation and simple linear regression for modeling relationships, and chi-square tests for analyzing categorical data commonly found in biological studies.

This course is ideal for:

Biology and agriculture majors planning research projects or graduate studies
Students needing to understand statistical methods in scientific literature
Anyone seeking practical data analysis skills for the life sciences

Lab Description:
Weekly lab sessions provide hands-on practical experience analyzing biological and agricultural datasets using R software. Students will learn essential skills including data importation and management, performing statistical tests, creating informative visualizations, and interpreting statistical outputs. Through guided exercises and practical examples, students will gain the analytical skills necessary for modern research in the life sciences.
課程目標:
On successful completion of this course, students will be able to:

Summarize and visualize biological data using descriptive statistics and effective graphs.
Understand and apply probability theory and probability distributions to biological contexts.
Recognize appropriate sampling techniques and apply the Central Limit Theorem.
Conduct hypothesis testing and construct confidence intervals for statistical inference.
Compare treatment effects using ANOVA and assess relationships with correlation and simple linear regression.
Analyze categorical data and genetic ratios using chi-square tests.
Use R software to perform data analysis, create visualizations, and interpret statistical outputs.
Communicate statistical results effectively and apply statistical thinking to real-world problems in biology and agriculture.

課名: 生物數據分析的計算技能
開課系所: 農藝學系 / 生物統計學程 / 生物統計學組
上課地點: 生物產業自動化中心(鄭江樓505室)
課程概述:
Contemporary biology and agricultural research routinely involves large-scale datasets generated by advancing technology. Proficiency in fundamental computational skills is required to conduct high-quality analysis and reproducible research across multiple disciplines. This course will introduce fundamental and transferable computational skills for working with biological data, enabling students to efficiently process and analyze large amounts of data in modern research environments.

Core topics include: command line interface, software version control (Git and GitHub) for collaboration, relational databases (MySQL and SQLite), and programming practices (testing, validation, and code quality). Practical skills will be developed through hands-on exercises and assignments.

Additional topics for background awareness include: continuous integration/continuous deployment (CI/CD) with GitHub Actions, high-performance computing (HPC) and cluster computing, cloud computing platforms, advanced programming tools (debugging with VS Code, linting, code profilers), and career paths in computational research. These topics will be covered at an overview level to provide awareness of modern computational infrastructure and advanced workflows.

Preparation for Advanced Studies: These foundational skills serve as prerequisites for advanced coursework in statistical analysis, machine learning, and AI-driven research methods, establishing the computational infrastructure necessary for specialized training in data science, bioinformatics, and computational modeling. While these skills are broadly transferable across disciplines, course examples and applications will focus on biological data and agricultural research contexts.

This course is ideal for:

Students and researchers in life sciences preparing for data-intensive research
Students planning to pursue advanced studies in bioinformatics, computational biology, or data science
Anyone working with biological datasets who needs to improve efficiency and reproducibility in their analyses
課程目標:
At the completion of this course, students will be able to:

Work with the command line interface to navigate file systems, manipulate files and directories, and execute commands to automate routine tasks efficiently.
Utilise software version control systems to manage code changes, collaborate effectively with team members, and maintain reproducible research workflows.
Understand and apply relational database concepts to design schemas, query data effectively, and manage large datasets for research applications.
Apply programming practices including writing unit tests for validation, implementing error handling, and creating clear documentation for research code.
Select and justify appropriate computational tools and approaches for common biological data analysis tasks based on data characteristics and research objectives.
Demonstrate awareness of modern computational infrastructure including CI/CD pipelines, HPC environments, and collaborative research workflows.
課程要求:
Language of Instruction: This course will be conducted entirely in English, including all lectures, course materials, and assignments.
Academic Integrity: Students are expected to maintain the highest standards of academic integrity. Cheating and plagiarism in any form of assessment are considered serious academic misconduct and will be handled according to university policy. All submitted work must be your own.
Prerequisites - Statistics: Basic statistics knowledge is required. Any Statistics 101 course covering descriptive statistics, simple linear regression, and ANOVA is sufficient.
Prerequisites - Programming: Functional knowledge of R OR Python is required, including: declaring variables, basic arithmetic operations, and basic data types (R: vectors, lists, data frames; Python: lists, dictionaries). Familiarity with declaring functions is beneficial but not required. Students will choose one primary language for the course.
Computer Requirements: Students are strongly encouraged to have access to a personal computer or laptop with administrator privileges. Software requirements and installation instructions will be provided throughout the course as needed.

本課程亦預期學生本課程中，在理解資訊、思考、思考後的決策，以及與他人交流自己的想法等層面上有所增長。這些能力是每位育種從業人員及和社會中堅所必備的。

課程概述: Factorial designs are widely used in agricultural, chemical, industrial and pharmaceutical studies. The objective of this course is to provide a rigorous and systematic treatment of theoretical aspects of factorial designs. Several important concepts in factorial experiments, such as treatment and block structures, effect aliasing and estimability, will be introduced. Design optimality criteria and construction methods will also be introduced to get efficient factorial designs. After successfully completing this course, students will be able to (1) understand the fundamental theory of factorial designs; (2) construct efficient fractional factorial designs; and (3) design factorial experiments to address real-world research questions.

課名: 壓電振動能量擷取導論
開課系所: 應用力學研究所 / 奈米工程與科學博士學位學程 / 奈米工程與科學碩士學位學程
課程概述:
能量擷取乃是將環境中潛在能源轉化為電能，並加以儲存、利用之技術。隨著低功率消耗電路的開發，能量擷取技術已是自我供電系統中不可或缺的一環。本課程將簡介壓電振動能量轉換儲存系統，即利用環境中的轉動或震動等動能，透過壓電能量擷取器，將機械振動能轉換為電能並加以儲存。一個完整的壓電能量擷取系統，大致上可分為高效能傳遞能量的振動子、高機電轉換之壓電材料與能量儲存電路等三個主要部分。因此本課程內容涵蓋了壓電力學與材料、振動、控制與電力電子等，將以基本觀念學習為主，並配合壓電模擬軟體(COMSOL，MULTIPHYSICS)與電路軟體 (PSpice) 教學，以加強整體觀念。故會從頭教起，因此非常歡迎大學部與研究所同學選修本課程。

    另外有兩個新的主題想在課堂分享。一是壓電感測元件電壓時域轉頻率域的訊號處理，並搭配卷積神經網路分類器，進行結構或設備狀態監控。二是摩擦式奈米發電機 (Triboelectric Nanogenerator，TENG)，其原理與壓電貼片感測元件有類似之處，因此若時間允許將作初步介紹。
課程目標: 對壓電振動能量擷取有一統合性認識與掌握。

課程概述: There are three chapters in this course. Chapter one covers the Cartesian Tensors, which are extensively used in the courses of Elasticity, Plasticity, Fluid mechanics, and other science subjects. Chapter two includes three parts. The first part introduces the existence and uniqueness theory for a system of 1st order ordinary differential equations (ODE). The second part covers the solution of a system of linear 1st order ODE, which is particular useful for the course of Dynamics. The third part is designed to solve linear 2nd order ODE with unknown source functions. We introduce the concepts of Dirac delta function, generalized functions, adjoint operators, Green’s functions and the integral representation of the solution of 2nd order ODE.  Chapter 3 also includes three parts. The 1st part introduces the classification of  the 2nd order partial differential equations (PDE). The 2nd part introduces the Green’s function and the integral representation of solution of 2nd order linear PDE. Free space Green’s functions are solved first for infinite domain and then method of images is introduced for solving some PDE with simple finite domains. The 3rd part introduces the eigenvalue problem of self-adjoint boundary value problems of 2nd order PDE, and the full or partial eigenfunction expansion for solving the linear 2nd order BVP or IBVP. Also included in this part are the Maximum-Minimum principle and unique theorems for Laplace/Poisson equation.

543 M5110 彈性力學一

Introduction
When a body is subjected to external loads, internal stress is induced in the body and the body deforms accordingly. If the body restores its original shape as the external loads are removed, it is called an elastic body. On the other hand, if the loading is so large such that permanent deformation takes place, the response of the body is inelastic. Usually engineering materials are designed to behave in the elastic range. The objective of the course is to discuss methods that can be used to analyze the stress and deformation of elasitic bodies under external loading. 

Prerequisite courses
Mechanics of materials
Applied mathematics: differential equations, tensor, complex variables

Course outline：
1.	Introduction (0.5 week)
2.	Kinematics of Deformation (2.5 weeks)
3.	Stress Analysis (2 weeks)
4.	Constitutive Laws (1 week)
5.	Formulation of Elasticity Problems (1.5 weeks)
6.	One-Variable Problems (2 weeks)
7.	Two-Dimensional Problems (3.5 weeks)
8.	Torsion Problems (1.5 weeks)
9.	Bending Problems (2 weeks)
課程目標:
Course objectives
The students should acquire the following knowledge as the semester ends:
1.	various measures to describe the deformation of a body, the physical meanings and the transformation of these measures, and compatibility condtions of strains.
2.	relation between stress vector and stress tensor; equations of motion, principal stress, and maximum shearing stress.
3.	hyperelastic materials and the generalized Hooke’s law, isotropic materials, and the relation between elastic constants and engineering constants.
4.	formulation of elasticity problems in rectangular, cylindrical, and spherical coordinate systems, and the principle of virtual work.
5.	analysis of problems with only on independent variables, such as a spherical shell subjected to internal pressure. 
6.	analysis of plane strain and plane stress problems, and the airy stress function.
7.	analysis of torsion problems.
8.	analysis of bending problems and the Timoshenko beam theory.

5.Special topic: Cell-based chip for biotechnology - bioreactors, studies of mechanics of abnormal cells, cell sorting, cell trapping.

課程概述:
黏彈機械性質(簡稱黏彈性)是材料機械性質的一種分類。世界上全部的材料，包括生物組織、生醫材料、工程材料(橡膠、高分子聚合物、混凝土、金屬…)、自然界中的材料(岩石、土壤、木材…)、食物等等，都是黏彈性的，只有黏彈性程度多寡的差別。
材料的黏彈性，會大大決定材料的mechanical behaviors(即材料在受到外力時的stress和strain)、與材料在運作或應用時的表現。譬如，一條肌腱在運動時會不會撕裂甚至斷掉、一個橡膠墊片在長期使用的過程中會不會太早壞掉、一塊木材適不適合用來製作椅子、一顆芭樂好不好吃等等，很大部分都取決於材料的黏彈性。因此，測量並瞭解材料的黏彈性、瞭解黏彈性材料的mechanical behaviors，在許多工程與科學領域都具有重要的應用價值。除此之外，日常生活、自然界中的許多現象都和黏彈性有關。
有別於理想線性彈性材料的單純，黏彈性材料的mechanical behaviors相當特殊且千變萬化，因此如果想正確測量材料的黏彈性，需要先瞭解黏彈性力學的基本觀念、學理基礎，如此才能瞭解、掌握材料黏彈性的測量與分析方法。
本課程的主旨是希望學生在修習本課程後，能瞭解材料黏彈性與黏彈性力學的基本觀念、學理基礎，並具備材料黏彈性之測量與分析的工程實務能力、黏彈性力學相關的基礎電腦模擬與分析能力，與進一步閱讀相關資料文獻、做相關研究與技術研發的能力。

課程內容：
第一章、黏彈性的基本觀念與實驗測量方法
第二章、微分型式之黏彈數學模型
第三章、積分型式之黏彈數學模型
第四章、黏彈性之動態測量方法
額外學習單元、曲線擬合之基礎與實務
課程目標:
以實務應用的角度而言，本課程的目標是要使學生學會一個方法學：如何測量並分析材料的黏彈性。
本課程的設計方式，即是一步步地引導學生學會這個方法學(即下述之前四點)；修習完本課程後，學生將具有分析材料黏彈性的能力、瞭解實驗測驗材料黏彈性的原理、與黏彈性力學相關的基礎電腦模擬與分析能力。

開課系所: 人類學系 / 臺灣研究學程
課程概述:
本課程為考古學領域中的區域研究，以台灣及其周邊為專題，介紹台灣的考古學史，以及以台灣史前史為主的研究成果。
台灣考古學的開始一般被認定為1896年，早期多為探險式的遺址發現調查，後期才見機關團體進行系統性的調查與研究，在日本學者主導約五十年的時間奠定了台灣考古學的基礎。到1950年代前後，大陸中國學者來台，帶來中國考古學的歷史研究方法，確立了台灣考古學的文化史研究方向。1970年代以後，留學生陸續引進西方的新知識，讓今日的台灣考古學更加多元。
台灣史前史始於更新世晚期的舊石器時代，當時人類藉由冰河時期的陸橋從東亞大陸步行進入台灣島。新石器時代又有大量的移民帶來新的技術與生活方式，在台灣各地深入適應與發展，形成特有的文化面貌。到了兩千年前，鐵器的出現取代了長久以來的石器，導致生活方式的劇烈改變。鐵器時代也是與外界大量進行物資交換的時代，從這個接觸過程中，台灣住民學得了新知識與新技術。到了十七世紀則是由貿易帶來文化的接觸與影響。雖然地處海島，但是史前以來的台灣便不斷地透過各種方式吸收外來要素，並融合於多樣的本島文化之中。因此，史前台灣和其周邊地區有著緊密的關係，認識我們周邊地區的發展亦是了解台灣的重要管道。
經由考古學者們的研究，上述的過程逐漸清晰，然而另方面也引來各種問題。本課程將以這些學術疑問為前導，藉其思考，說明台灣史前史。
無論從學史角度或台灣史前發展脈絡來看，台灣考古學皆有其獨特性質，此為台灣考古研究須把握的基礎。而本初級課程兼具「考古學」與「台灣研究學程」等兩項目標，具體而言，主要期待在於讓同學藉此深入台灣的非文字歷史，以及台灣之考古學研究概況。
課程目標:
1. 了解台灣考古學研究史的發展、學界目前對於臺灣史前暨歷史時代生活樣貌的認識，以及仍在議論中的諸多相關問題。
2. 認識台灣史前暨歷史時代的物質文化。
3. 奠基於以上基礎，能夠對研究史上各種爭論的本質有所認識，並能引用相關資料說明自己的觀點。

閱讀民族誌如同閱讀小說一般，可作為人類系學生的基本素養。本課希望鼓勵學生藉由閱讀不同文類(genres)與理論意涵的民族誌，進而培養欣賞原典、練習口頭報告、讀書心得撰寫與提問的能力，並透過民族誌閱讀了解人類學的全貌觀視野。

課名: 青銅器時代的文明：愛琴海和近東
開課系所: 人類學系 / 經典人文學程
課程概述: This course is designed to provide students with a sound knowledge of key theories and archaeological evidence that lie at the core of research in the cross-cultural studies between the East and West in the 2nd millennium BC. It builds upon anthropology, archaeology and prehistory to consider the age of palace-based civilizations in Egypt, Levant, Hittite Anatolia, Mycenaean Greece, Minoan Crete and Cyprus. It ensures students gain an understanding of different theoretical perspectives. It provides an insight into the social impact of processes such as the intensification of trade; social acceptance of technological innovation; the integration of disparate economies, centralization, culture contact, exchange, world-system theory and environmental change. Students will gain knowledge and understanding of the development of western attitudes to other cultures; the manner in which interdisciplinary studies can lead to much richer reconstructions and socio-political developments in the Aegean and Near East. The aim of the module is to show the cosmopolitanism and international relations between states and palaces and the changing understanding of civilization through the rise and decline of European colonialism.

課名: 文化資產保存的理論與實踐
開課系所: 人類學系 / 人類學研究所
課程概述:
文化資產是人類過去各種心智活動的結果，具歷史、藝術、文化或科學等價值，提供我們探究與暸解過去人類心理、藝術、經濟、科技、社會等活動的種種面貌，其保存之重要性不言可喻。這門課程將介紹在不同的文化與時空背景下，文化資產保存理論與實踐之情形，並從多元的角度討論審視之。
文化資產保存跨越不同學科領域，不僅僅包含技術層面的問題，更涉及觀念或哲學層面的問題。一座古蹟或一件古物，如何保存，是否需要修復，或修復到何種面貌，都與古蹟或古物所在的時空脈絡下如何被詮釋或被賦予的意義有關。而東西方各自有不同的文化背景，原有的文化資產保存的傳統亦有異。而在全球化潮流的影響下，保存的觀念與技術不斷修正，差異也逐漸縮小。這種演化的過程如何呈現在保存的具體實踐中，亦是我們探討的對象。
這門課程內容包含對文化資產特質與範疇的界定、介紹討論保存與修復的歷史、修復理論、憲章、宣言以及其他相關的歷史文獻。有關修復與真實性的問題，以及保存與修復倫理，亦是這門課關注的重點。而保存政策與法規的制定，經常規範了文化資產保存的實踐方向，自然不能忽略之。
要掌握文化資產保存的全貌，除了暸解觀念、理論或政策層面的相關議題外，對有關的實務與技術層面的基本認識亦不可或缺。本課程亦將介紹之。
最後，我們將實際透過一些東西方具體的保存案例，討論其理論與實踐層面的各種意涵。
課程目標: 這門課除能增進修課同學有關保存的相關知識外，也培養同學在日後面對文化資產時，能有更寬廣的觀察視野與思考面向。
課程要求: 這門課涵蓋的範圍極廣，要求同學必須在上課前先閱讀指定的相關材料，以便能在上課中參與討論。

課程概述:
本課程是環境人類學的進階課程，以當代重要的環境議題為主題，探討其所涉及的社會文化與政治經濟因素，並且希望在閱讀中思索以人類學知識應用於環境行動的可能途徑。

本學期課程將以Marisol de la Cadena的研究為主題，作為她將於六月初訪臺的前置共學，期望能透過這門課程的閱讀與討論，帶大家進入多重世界的民族誌實驗。Marisol de la Cadena 為UC-Davis人類學系教授，是安第斯地區人類學研究的代表性學者。其理論發展受到 Donna Haraway、John Law、Marilyn Strathern、Eduardo Viveiros de Castro 與 Isabelle Stengers 等思想家的啟發，並與 Mario Blaser 共同推動「政治本體論」（political ontology）與「多重宇宙」（pluriverse）等跨學科研究路徑。她的代表作 Earth Beings: Ecologies of Practice Across Andean Worlds（2015）以具實驗性的民族誌書寫，挑戰自然／文化、知識客體／知識主體等現代性所建構的二元對立。透過與兩位安第斯智者 Mariano 與 Nazario 的長期對話，她探索多重本體世界之間的差異、交纏與不可共量性。在書寫策略上，de la Cadena將前述學者提出的equivocation、cosmopolitics等概念落實於民族誌實踐，具體示範了如何回應當前田野工作的核心挑戰--當面對非人存有者參與構作的世界，以及其間不可共量的差異時，田野調查與書寫便無法僅止於對「異文化」的轉譯與詮釋，而必須在複數世界之間進行具倫理感知與政治敏感度的交涉。

Earth Beings 兼具高度的田野厚度與理論密度，閱讀難度不低，因此我們設計了這門共讀課程，以本書為核心，搭配各章節的相關理論文獻，作為迎接 de la Cadena 六月初來訪的準備。期望經過一學期的密集閱讀與討論，對她的研究所涉及的區域背景與理論脈絡建立充分的理解，才能在她來訪時進行實質而深入的對話交流。

從環境人類學的問題意識觀之，Earth Beings既是一本關於人與「環境」（土地、山、水等「自然環境」）之關係的民族誌，也是一本批判「環境」這個概念的理論書籍。我們將從環境人類學晚近三個相互關聯的主題來閱讀與定位本書：超越人類的世界（more-than-human worlds）、針對開採主義與全球環境論述的原住民批判，以及本體論政治與國家環境治理的辯證。
課程目標:
本課程以 Earth Beings 為核心讀本，並嘗試從更廣闊的知識脈絡理解 de la Cadena 所介入的理論與實踐現場。結構安排如下：

1.	首先，在深入進入本書之前，我們將先回顧環境人類學稍早的思想脈絡，特別是自然／文化二元論的建構與解構、多於人的存有與世界構作，以及開採主義批判研究，以了解de la Cadena 在本書所回應的學術議題。
2.	其次，課程的主體部分將對 Earth Beings 進行多週的細讀與概念拆解，並在此過程中逐步引介 de la Cadena 立基的兩個關鍵民族誌概念：equivocation 與 ethnographic cosmopolitics。
3.	最後，完成本書的細讀之後，我們將轉向 de la Cadena 近期的學術作品，並援引其他具代表性的文獻進行對話，思考她的研究對環境民族誌、環境人文，以及原住民政治的啟發與貢獻。

課名: 東亞與東南亞考古文化遺產中的政治與國家主義
開課系所: 人類學系 / 東亞研究學分學程 / 人類學研究所
課程概述:
This course explores archaeological cultural heritage in East and Southeast Asia and how material remains of past human behavior in this broad region play an active role in shaping human perceptions of self and others in the present day. Archaeological cultural heritage as an academic field and as a profession is rapidly evolving in East and SE Asia, with governmental policy making, political motivations such as nation-building and nationalistic agendas, globalization, economic expansion and development, and many other factors shaping choices for how and why archaeological sites, objects, architecture, and landscapes are preserved, protected, and presented. This course will focus on these political roles of archaeological cultural heritage and examine them in conceptual and theoretical terms using a necessarily anthropological, interdisciplinary approach with models and methods from archaeology, critical museology, material cultural theory, postcolonial theory, and memory studies, among others. Case studies from around East and Southeast Asia, including Taiwan, mainland China, Korea, Japan, the Philippines, Thailand, Cambodia, Laos, Indonesia, and Malaysia will serve to provide insight into the relationship between archaeological heritage and nationalism and allow us to explore such related issues as the domination of Eurocentrism in heritage practice and theory (and see new alternatives arising); heritage's role in identity and ideology; contested ownership; commodification and value; memorialization and "dark heritage" (e.g., post-conflict or post-trauma sites); indigenous and minority rights and stakeholding; the impact of looting and the illicit antiquities trade; and heritage tourism.

This course is open to upper-level undergraduates and MA students (學士班高年級及碩士班). This course is conducted in English, with English-language readings and written assignments.
課程目標: This seminar-style course will familiarize upper-level undergraduate and Masters students with current issues in archaeological cultural heritage in East and Southeast Asia. Through case studies from the region, students will become familiar with key concepts and issues in the region and gain a critical understanding of the interrelationships between political motivations in the present and the reconstruction and presentation of the archaeological past(s) as cultural heritage.
課程要求:
Students are required to attend all class meetings since this will be a mostly seminar-style course featuring group discussion. Should you have a proper excuse for having to miss class (such as illness or major school-related event for which you can provide a letter) please notify the instructor in advance. Students should be prepared to fully participate in class and should complete the assigned readings before the class meeting. There will be student presentations and student-lead discussions, which contribute to your final grade. Students will sign-up to be a discussion leader for certain weeks: they will also give a short presentation on themes and issues derived from the readings that week before leading the class in discussion.

Research paper:  The final research paper required for the course is due January 11. This paper should be 10-15 pages in length for undergraduates and 15-20 pages for graduate students. You will choose your own topic and consult with the teacher for approval. You must develop a research topic and hand in a title and one paragraph description of what you will research and discuss, along with 4 references, by December 1. I encourage you to submit an outline of your research paper at least three weeks before the paper due date so that we can discuss its strengths and weaknesses. I will be happy to discuss with you any aspects of the process of researching and writing your paper, and properly citing your sources, and we will discuss this in class, as well. Late papers will only be accepted with a grading penalty.

課程概述: This course is a seminar for advanced undergraduate, MA, and PhD students, taught in English. We will focus on a variety of issues concerning the archaeology of the prehistoric period in China (Paleolithic and Neolithic periods) and explore some of the key research themes for these time periods and the multidisciplinary approaches used to gain understanding of them. Topics can include human evolution, Paleolithic lithic technology and new approaches to it, Eurocentric biases in modeling human behavior in East Asia, the Upper Paleolithic Revolution, Early Pottery production, the origins of agriculture, settlement pattern studies, ritual and funerary practices, bioarchaeological studies of demography and health, Neolithic stone tool and pottery production, the pathway toward social complexity, craft specialization, etc. We will also look at regional developments and models of cultural interaction. The time period covered begins with the earliest archaeological sites and hominid fossils (at least 1.6 million years ago) and ends with the Longshan period (ca. 2500-1900 BC). We will focus not on a textbook approach, but rather on recent research papers related to a specific topic, with the goal of understanding major issues in Chinese Paleolithic and Neolithic archaeology and the current state of research, as well as new discoveries and research innovations (particularly with the introduction of scientific methodologies and anthropological orientations). The topics we will cover are flexible, and we will decide as a class which to select. For each topic, we can read “classic” papers and/or look critically at recent publications and how they introduce new ideas and approaches, so we can see the “state of the art” in the field.
課程目標: Students taking this course will gain an understanding of key issues and methodologies in the most recent research on the archaeology of the Paleolithic and Neolithic periods in China. Drawing on case studies from China, students will gain knowledge of the multidisciplinary approaches used in the scientific and anthropological archaeological study of prehistoric human societies and the ability to critically evaluate research approaches, methodologies, assumptions, and results.
課程要求: As this is a seminar student, students must do all of the assigned readings before class and then participate fully in the seminar discussions. Each student will be assigned one week in which he/she will be the discussion leader and must prepare a brief overview of that week’s topics and prepare comments and questions to the class on the readings.

課程概述: 臺灣是海島國家，海岸地帶過往依海的生計方式，發展出獨特的漁業文化。但相較於農村研究，人類學界以漁業及海洋社群為研究主題的著作較少，自經典民族誌《龜山島》（王崧興1967）之後，就很少見到漁業與漁村研究的人類學作品。本課程藉由文本閱讀與田野踏查，引介同學認識重要的海洋/漁業人類學研究，以及有別於陸地世界分析的理論工具，期能更深入了解漁業勞動、漁業技術、漁村社會、人-海關係等面向的傳統與變遷。
課程目標:
1.以文化人類學的方法與理論來探索海洋與漁業議題。
2.了解依海人群的獨特生活方式。
3.反思當代面臨的海洋環境問題，以及人類學能夠做什麼。

課程概述: 這門「考古材料的介紹與科學分析」是選修課程，目的是在幫助學生瞭解考古材料與科學分析。考古學是通過分析過去的社會遺留下來的物質文化來研究人類的歷史。本課程旨在向學生介紹科技考古學的基礎理論、方法、目的和分析技術。本課程介紹了基於化學、物理和地質學的科學方法及其在無機考古材料（如石器、陶瓷、金屬和玻璃材料）分析中的應用，涵蓋了材料結構、原材料和生產過程的基礎知識。同時，本課程的考古案例研究將涵蓋歐亞非區域的史前到歷史時期。

●	獲得解釋特定考古材料的知識和技能；
●	評估科學方法對考古材料分析的相關性和適用性；

課程概述: 人類飲食相關的考古學研究源遠流長。作為飲食用具的陶器，往往是遺址中出土數量最為豐富的遺物之一，也是考古學研究最為廣泛的材料類型。而陶器的本質即為與飲食活動密切相關的日常器具，其使用情境指向食物的準備、烹煮與食用過程，也促使考古學研究由器物本身，進一步關注飲食行為及其社會意涵。一方面，食物作為維繫人類生存的基本需求，提供身體運作所需的營養與能量；另一方面，食物的取得、準備、烹煮、食用與棄置──亦即所謂的 foodways（飲食方式）──則蘊含豐富的社會與文化意涵。在此脈絡下，考古學對飲食的研究取向，已由早期著重食物本身的辨識與性質分析，逐步擴展至對飲食相關行為及其社會意義的探討。在此脈絡下，本課程從物質文化的視角出發，我們探討自史前至當代的飲食實踐，並分析食物的生產、烹飪與消費等行為，如何參與並形塑人類社會與文化。
課程目標:
1.	理解foodways的概念與理論意涵，認識飲食實踐在社會與文化中的角色。
2.	學習飲食相關考古學的相關材料與研究，培養進階研究的興趣。
3.	建立透過物質文化分析飲食行為並建構考古詮釋的能力，發展提出研究問題與進行資料分析之基礎能力。

課程概述:
這門課程旨在勾勒自宇宙大爆炸以迄未來可能情境的人類宏大歷程。課程由人類學、歷史與文學領域的專家團隊共同教授，將以跨學科的視角探討兩個根本性問題：「人類如何走到今日？」以及「人類將走向何方？」本課程將聚焦於一系列具轉折意義的歷史與文化事件——自意識的演化、全球文明的形構，直至迫近的未來發展——以理解長久以來塑造人類於地球生存之各種動力。

本課程強調，學習人類整體的歷程能夠培養獨特的謙卑與責任意識。透過理解地質與宇宙時間的浩瀚廣闊，學員將更清楚地看見個體生命的有限性，以及人類當前所掌握的前所未有之力量。我們可能是當代改變全球氣候與生物體系的主要物種，此現象因此被稱為「人類世」（Anthropocene）。本課程將引導學員在這種雙重視角下，思考並培養對地球生命長遠未來的守護意識。
本課分為三大專題，分別由人類學系、歷史學系及外文系負責進行課程教授。
課程目標:
獲得新的視角：將我們當下的處境置於地質與宇宙時間的浩瀚尺度之中，認識到人類文明既短暫亦脆弱。
理解人類影響：認識在「人類世」（Anthropocene）中，我們這一物種所掌握的前所未有之力量，以及這種力量對於地球生命未來所要求的守護責任。
運用跨學科方法：透過整合人文與社會科學的洞見，分析複雜的人類相關議題。
批判性思考人類：超越單一化的人類定義，培養對我們這一物種的多元性與潛能更為細緻而深刻的理解。
專題一：文明的另類視角：考古學的觀點（人類學系）
本專題將以考古學的角度重新理解何謂文明？人類這一物種從約20萬年前出現在非洲大陸後，透過與不同物種的互動，漸漸形塑出當代的文明。考古學透過各種多於人的研究，重新爬梳這段以人為中心的歷史論述，看到在這文明發展的過程中，不同人、非人物種及物在這之間的不同貢獻及限制。
專題二：世界文明與人類歷史變遷 （歷史系）
本專題規劃探討「世界文明」的形塑，和從此角度探討人類歷史變遷，及相關議題與當今世界的關係。「世界文明」是一個統稱，當今對人類多元世界的認知，早已超出少數幾個標誌文明的定義，然隨著人文社會科學從各種專業探索人類歷史和全球化，世界文明是一個豐富多樣的領域，「文明」的概念在近十幾年也有很多的批判性省思。世界各地從歷史發展角度，如何經歷接觸和衝突，才達成今日的全球化，為本課程的主軸。單元主題包括歐洲海外擴張史中的貿易和傳教、美洲、非洲、和亞洲與歐洲海外勢力發展的互動、19-20世紀西方霸權的興起和問題、和跨文化接觸特定案例的討論，亦包括關於文化交流的研究方法等。

課程概述:
台灣的考古研究至今超過百年，具體共發現超過2,000處以上的考古遺址。研究者們藉由各種考古調查、發掘、實驗研究等方法，目前約略可建構出台灣的史前史。一般認為，舊石器時代約從距今3萬年前開始，當時人類集中出現於東部海岸，以狩獵、採集維生；新石器時代約從距今6千年開始，主要特徵是有農業，並據此發展出較複雜的生活方式與社會組織；距今約2千年開始為鐵器時代，主要特徵為鐵器的技術利用，以及對外的交換、貿易活動。整體而言，台灣史前文化的變化在各地域間有共通性，在時間向度上有持續性，並和近代的原住民文化有緊密的關係。以上雖然仍有很多疑問，但隨著新資料不斷的被發現，研究成果日趨豐富。
    本課程上課資料主要包括前人的研究成果，以及新的考古學發現等兩類。同學們可藉由結合這兩項資料的重新討論，再加上使用學術上的新思維，以建立具有自己觀點的台灣史前史。此外，相較於以文字史學為基礎的歷史，主要由考古學建立的史前史顯然具有較多社會科學的成分，所以也鼓勵同學盡量可從不同學科的角度來思考各種主題。例如「本島的文化特質」、「外來文化的影響」、「與原住民文化之關係」、「南島語族」等議題，期待同學們對台灣史前史能有新的自我創見。
    課程預計區分為六大單元，分別是最早台灣人的出現、台灣新石器時代的形態、台灣的史前農業、外來異文化的影響、台灣的南島語族特性、原住民族群的形成過程等。各單元內容詳見下述的「課程進度與週次」。
    上課形式為專題教學、論文研讀、群組討論。
課程目標:
1.認識台灣史前考古的重要發現與研究。
2.思考台灣史前人與文化的特性。
3.認識史前文化與原住民的關係。
4.思考創新建立台灣史前史。

課名: 醫療人類學與全球衛生
開課系所: 人類學系 / 人類學研究所
課程概述:
This course explores the field of global health, examining epidemic disease and health care dilemmas, through the unique lens of anthropology. We will ask some of the following questions: How can the knowledge and methodological approach of medical anthropology contribute to both researching and addressing the health concerns of the disadvantaged? In what ways does anthropology’s attention to culture not only enrich our understanding of the conditions and dynamics of global health? How can it help us to engage with and think critically about global health interventions? Throughout the course, students will be encouraged to think creatively and critically about health problems and policies as well as scrutinize the value systems that underlie the discipline of global health itself.

This course is organized into two parts. In the first part, we will examine the social conditions behind epidemic disease, the emergence of the field of global health, and the humanitarian spirit that has inspired global health activists. In the second part, we will explore the persistent challenges and uncertainties that continue to thwart the ideals of global health, from environmental racism, to institutional disparities, to public apprehensions. However, we will conclude with the hopeful perspective that both global health activists and anthropologists bring to this field.
課程目標:
At the end of the course, the students are expected to be able to:
1. reflect critically on the origins of global health
2. demonstrate basic understanding of the social roots to epidemic disease
3. demonstrate critical perspective on the challenges of global health and the possibilities of anthropological work in this field

課名: 運動：樂趣與暴力，競爭與社會性
開課系所: 人類學系 / 人類學研究所
課程概述:
Few activities in the lives of ordinary people around the world bring together physicality, emotions, politics, money, and morality as dramatically as sport. Whether in Brazil’s huge soccer stadiums or parks in China, on baseball diamonds in Taiwan or rugby fields in Fiji, or in wrestling arenas in Senegal, human beings test their physical limits, invest emotional energy, bet money, perform witchcraft, ingest substances, and display what they think is important in life.

Sport plays a tremendously important role in setting boundaries between groups, contesting them, defining what is normal and what is extraordinary, and entangling the everyday life of ordinary people with the state, the nation, and the global. Thus, while sport is easy to dismiss as an inconsequential aspect of our lives, on closer inspection it emerges as a microcosm of what life is about. To borrow a phrase from Émile Durkheim, one of the founders of the modern social sciences, sport provides a window onto “the serious life.”
課程目標:
Sport brings together seemingly incompatible aspects of human existence, such as pleasure and violence, competition and sociality, work and leisure, hierarchy and equality, and morality and corruption. It is thus a particularly productive lens through which we can explore many of the topics that are of interest to anthropologists and other social scientists, and this course explores what we can learn about broad questions in anthropology through the lens of sport.

At the end of the course, students will be able to:
•	Understand how anthropologists approach the study of sport.
•	Analyze how sport functions as political practice and as a resource in struggles over power, belonging, and identity.
•	Connect the anthropology of sport to broader debates in socio-cultural anthropology and other social sciences.

課名: 論文研究計畫進階討論
課程概述:
研究計畫的撰寫是人類學與考古學研究的重要起點。無論是田野工作、檔案研究、實驗分析或社群合作計畫，研究計畫皆是研究者將理論關懷、材料基礎與方法設計進行整合與具體化的過程。透過計畫書的書寫，研究者不僅梳理自身的問題意識，也必須清楚說明研究與既有文獻的對話關係、材料取得的可能性，以及田野實踐與倫理考量。這一過程同時是一種反思，使研究構想由模糊走向具體。
然而，研究計畫並非固定不變的藍圖。特別在人類學與考古學的研究脈絡中，田野條件、社群互動、材料保存狀況與行政制度等因素，皆可能影響研究的進行。研究計畫的修正與調整，正是研究深化與成熟的表現。理解研究計畫的彈性與限制，是學術訓練的重要一環。
研究計畫的撰寫亦涉及不同情境與目的：可能是為學位論文提出整體研究設計，亦可能為申請發掘許可、研究經費或跨單位合作而撰寫。不同類型的計畫書有其特定的審查標準與論述重點，例如研究問題的明確性、理論定位的清晰度、方法與材料的對應關係、研究倫理與社群關係的安排，以及時間與資源的可行性。本課程將引導學生理解這些差異，並學習如何在不同制度與實踐脈絡中調整寫作策略。
課程目標: 本課程透過講授、指定閱讀、案例分析與實作練習，協助學生建立研究計畫撰寫的基本能力。課程內容包括：研究問題的形成、文獻回顧的策略性建構、理論架構與材料分析的連結、方法設計與田野規劃、研究倫理與社群合作的考量，以及不同類型計畫書的閱讀與評析。期末目標為完成一份具體且可實際運用的研究計畫書，使學生在未來進行田野研究或申請相關計畫時，具備清晰的論述能力與實踐基礎。

課程概述:
The Anthropology of the Body is a dynamic and emerging subfield in anthropology. Its importance stems from the historical neglect of bodies in Western humanist scholarship. The seminar will focus on the materiality of the human body, as a critical nexus between the individual and the external world. Our task in this course will be two-fold: first, to interrogate the intellectual traditions that have led an impoverished understanding of the body, such as the dualism of the mind-body divide; and second, to explore anthropological and other theoretical writings about the body that enable us to envision alternative worlds and modes of existence.
We should be prepared to struggle with the material in this course. In the words of Gilles Deleuze, we will attempt to make the leap into the “plane of immanence.” But we should recognize that this leap may be partial and incomplete. Our goal is to develop a set of theoretical tools that we can carry with us beyond this course, so that we can continue this arduous, but in my opinion, immensely rewarding task in our everyday lives.

The literature on the body has proliferated and grown so rapidly that there are countless ways to design a course such as this. Our approach this semester will have three parts. In Part I, we will begin with critique, exploring the implications of the mind-body divide, and looking at key theorists who offer tools for thinking beyond it. In Part II, we will explore phenomenological approaches to perception and “post-humanist” investigations of the body and its relationship to the environment. In Part III, we will conclude with ethnographic explorations of alternative bodily practices – in our case, dance (capoeira) in Brazil and wrestling in India – to enhance our understanding of our new concepts and further develop our own research projects.
課程目標:
At the end of the course, the students are expected to be able to:
1. reflect critically on the mind-body dualism of the Western philosophical tradition
2. show basic understanding of phenomenological and post-humanist approaches to understanding the human body.
3. to engage with various theoretical approaches to the body in ethnographic research and writing.

課名: 全球化情境下的語言與互動
課程概述:
While the study of globalization and its constitutive or cognate processes (e.g., transnationalism, localization, modernity, diasporic dispersal) has commanded enormous attention in socio-cultural anthropology, linguistic anthropology only began to contribute significantly to these efforts in the last couple of decades, despite the fact that many issues with which linguistic anthropologists have been concerned all along are relevant to globalization. Part of the goal here is to contribute to a rapprochement between the two subfields by exploring how socio-cultural anthropological debates on globalization can shed light on topics of interest to linguistic anthropology, and how a sensitivity to language and interaction can inform our socio-cultural understanding of globalization.

Readings and discussion are inter-disciplinary, almost by necessity: the amount of work on language and globalization remains modest. However, I have tried to identify research that recognizes, at least tacitly, the value of the ethnographic analysis of lived experience. Some readings demonstrate a greater sophistication in the analysis of language or interaction than in the analysis of social context, while other authors will prove themselves to be more confident writing about globalization than about language or interaction. In all cases, we will seek to establish bridges between traditions of inquiry, areas of expertise, and ways of framing questions, seeking methodological connections and intellectual cross-fertilization.
課程目標:
Language offers powerful tools through which persons and groups throughout the world position themselves vis-à-vis globalization. Based on a critical reading of ethnographically informed and discourse-oriented works, this course explores ways in which analytic attention to language use can help us better understand the social, cultural, and political forces of globalization, and how an analysis of globalization can help us better understand the workings of language. 

Topics of relevance include the role of “international languages” in the industrializing world; the impact of new media and forms of communication on people’s lives; the hegemony of English in international contexts; the role of language ideology in a globalized political economy; the commodification of language skills in the neoliberal economy; and the politics of multilingualism, language attrition, and language revitalization. 

An examination of these topics through the lens of current theoretical trends (e.g., language ideology, language and political economy, critique of neoliberalism) will enable us to refine our understanding of the social dynamics involved in globalization and localization, field methods for the investigation of language in its social context, and the implications of this understanding for applied concerns.

At the end of the course, students will be able to:
•	Have an appreciation for how linguistic anthropology can contribute to our understanding of global processes
•	Have an appreciation for how the study of global processes can contribute to our understanding of language and interaction in social life
•	Be able to use the tools of linguistic anthropology in a research project on global processes

課程概述:
本課程以亞洲美術史中的經典作品為主題，透過繪畫、書法、宗教圖像與視覺文化等實例，探討作品在不同歷史情境中如何成為「經典」，以及其在後世的觀看與詮釋方式。課程結合作品分析與歷史背景，說明經典並非固定不變，而是隨時代與文化脈絡不斷被重新理解。

透過不同時期與地區作品的比較討論，課程引導學生思考藝術典範的形成因素，並關注經典作品在當代文化中的再詮釋，進而從藝術史角度反思自身與文化傳統的關係。
課程目標:
1. 引導學生認識亞洲美術史中的重要經典作品，理解其形成背景、歷史意義，以及在不同時代中的詮釋與運用方式。

2. 協助學生思考「經典」與藝術典範的建構過程，認識其所涉及的價值判斷與文化因素。

3. 培養學生透過作品觀察與分析，理解藝術與社會、思想及文化之間的關係，並從歷史角度反思自身的文化位置，嘗試將經典藝術與當代文化情境加以連結。

課程概述:
本課程目的為藉由剖析墓葬的發展與出土品藝術風格透視當代社會文化，主要材料為現今中國境內出土的墓葬。墓葬總能引起許多的想像，也經常是電視劇與小說的創作題材。但掀開浪漫想像後的墓葬是什麼樣子？能夠怎麼增進我們對過去的了解？本課程將以個案切入，依序介紹各時代的重要墓葬，以及學者如何透過墓葬蘊含的豐富訊息認識過去。

　　墓葬看似僅為死者而設，但墓中的物件與圖像乘載的不只有死者意向，還有喪家及製作者的意圖，乃至整個社會文化氛圍。可以說墓葬是介於生死之間的場域，也是多方意向協商下的成果。過去學界多重視墓中出土的個別材料，但近年來，學界轉向將墓葬視為一個整體來了解。本課程也採此取徑，每週由一座或一群墓葬切入，介紹墓葬形制與出土物，剖析當週案例蘊含的多重意義，藉此揭示不同時空下的人群對死後世界的想像與期望乃至孕育這種想望的社會文化，進而重新檢視當前對歷史上各朝代的印象。
課程目標:
1.	能用正確的專有名詞清楚說明各時代的墓葬形制與隨葬品特色。
2.	舉出現今中國境內的重要墓葬遺址發現，並清楚說明墓葬形制與隨葬品背後的社會文化。
3.	能藉由分析墓葬內的物質遺存呈現光憑文獻無法勾勒出的歷史。

課程概述: 本課程嘗試引導學生從閱讀論文、史料、以及實際考察（觀賞作品與實地踏查）的方式，來瞭解台灣近代美術史的各個面向。課程最初著眼於美術制度在台灣的移植與建立。先大致說明「美術」概念與制度移植到東亞的過程，並介紹作為台灣「美術」制度中最重要的美術展覽會。接下來的課程將從「人」的角度切入，藉由閱讀論文與史料，來嘗試理解與「台灣」有關，且具有代表性的藝術家及其創作，並分析在不同的脈絡與研究視角下，所形塑出來的藝術家像有何不同。

課程概述:
這學期的課程重點在討論日本導入最初的現代建築的思想與作品，（特別是受德國文化圈影響下表現主義與分離派建築），來看亞洲國（非西方國家）的建築現代建築起源問題。
教科書：田路貴浩編，《分離派建築会　日本のモダニズム建築誕生》，京都大学学術出版会，2020。
前言
田路 貴浩
1920(大正9)年、在東京帝国大学建築学科畢業的6位學生，名為石本喜久治、堀口捨己、山田守、瀧澤眞弓、森田慶一與矢田茂。他們以自己的畢業作品的展覽為契機，提倡從歴史様式分離的新建築的藝術性「創作」，組織成立了「分離派建築会」。他們還處在對建築設計實務尚未成熟的階段，即匆忙出航的青年，就因為是東京帝大畢業的大學生的「分離」運動，而受到高度的注目，也惹起了賛成與否定的兩極意見之爭論。
後來，他們在1928年以前，總共舉辦了七次展覧会。並且配合展出的作品提出論述，出版了作品集，於編輯了雜誌的特集專號。因為這些年輕建築師們並無法立即成熟地將自己的思想表現於建築作品上，因此為補足其缺陷，他們隨著設計作品熱情地利用論述提出自己的訴求。隨著活動的波紋的擴大，較為年輕的大内秀一郎、早稲田選科生的蔵田周忠、曾是逓信省営繕課製圖工設計的岡村蚊象(後來的山口文象)等人也加入了活動團隊，還有曾經以山田耕筰為師承學習作曲具有特殊經歷的川喜田煉七郎等人也加入了分離會，愈加增強了他們的影響力道。但是隨著運動前進的路經之清楚化，在1928年舉辦的第七次展覧会後不久，即宣布解散分離會，停止了相關的活動。
從第一次世界大戦開始，經歷関東大震災，到満州事変為止的快速變動的時代裡，也是大正民主時代的自由空氣曾經一時地覆蓋了整個社會的時期，藝術界充溢著清新的空氣，不斷地生成出新的潮流。分離派建築会的活動雖然不滿10個年頭，但是死命地追趕當時處於激烈變動之歐洲最前衛的建築潮流，開創寫下了日本近代建築史新的一頁歷史。自從團隊活動停止後的1930年代，個別的成員實現了包浩斯或是勒科比易帶頭創作出來無装飾的現代主義建築，建構了戰後建築界各領域的基礎。石本喜久治創設了今日仍持續活動，名為「大石設計」的大型設計事務所，山口文象也相同是RIA的創始者。山田守是廣為人知的日本武道館或是京都塔的設計者，也是東海大學建築學科的創設者。就大學的創設者而言，堀口捨己也創設了明治大學建築學科，他也茶室研究領域的開拓者的建築史研究者。森田慶一也翻譯了西洋最古的建築書維特魯威（Vitruvius）之建築書，留下了輝煌的研究業績，對日本接受西洋建築做出了偉大的貢獻。還有，蔵田周忠在武蔵工業大學(現在的東京都市大學)，而瀧澤眞弓則在大阪市立大學等地從事教育工作。
但是，他們所標榜的「分離」到底指的是什麼呢？在19世紀末的德語文化圈，從慕尼黑開始，各地的藝術家們舉出「Secession(分離派)」的旗幟，批判依然處於的學院派，開始以新藝術為目標的分離運動。其中在1897年，由古斯塔夫·克林姆（Gustav Klimt；1862-1918）帶頭而組成的「維也納分離派」（Vienna Secession），有奧托·華格納（Otto Wagner；1841-1918）及其弟子約瑟夫·奧爾布立稀（Joseph Olbrich；1867-1908）等人的建築家們也參與其中，分離派運動的波紋也傳到建築的領域。華格納早於維也納分離派，即擔任維也納美術學院（Akademie der bildenden Künste Wien）的教授，揭舉「藝術僅遵從必要」的座右銘，以都市計畫顧問的身份，實現了為數不少的作品於市鎮之中。還有，奧爾布立稀完成了維也納分離派専用展示館之分離派会館(1898)，大膽地導入了白色牆面，大大地刷新了装飾性的折衷主義，提出了新的建築様式。
至於日本「分離派建築会」的情形，雖然他們主張其與維也納、德國的分離派沒有關係，但是是受其影響應該是確定的。他們還將装飾性様式的折衷主義斷定為「過去建築圏」，宣示要從那裡分離。其「過去建築圏」是指明治政府致力導入的西洋建築。明治政府在維新後即強而有力地推動導入近代文明，但是到了日俄戰爭(1904-1905)戰勝後，也終於看到西洋列強諸国身影的背後。建築界也在1909(明治42)年，完成了完完全全屬於巴洛克樣式的赤坂離宮，換言之，在明治末年，日本完成學習様式建築的目標幾乎已經達成。在那同時，國民感情傾向了國家民族主義，興起了建造正式的帝國議會議院的熱潮。於是在1910(明治43)年，在日本建築學舉辦了以「我國（日本）未來應有建築様式」為題的討論會為最高潮，活潑地討論了日本要如何創造獨自的建築様式問題。在那個時候，也正是熱心介紹新藝術運動（Art nouveau）、分離派樣式（Secession）等新潮流進入日本，以及西洋歴史建築様式開始動搖，出現了種種折衷様式的時候。還有，當時也進行導入鋼骨結構與鋼筋混凝土結構，這些新的結構技術也幫助了新樣式的探索。進一步，在1917(大正6)年爆發了1917年俄國革命（Russian Revolution）對世界的衝擊也影響了日本建築界，建築師的關心從過去的官廳建築轉移至為民眾所需要實用性設施及住宅。
分離派建築會誕生，其實不限建築，有如上所述的國内外政治、社會局勢或是思想潮流激烈變動的時代背景存在。它並非是突然出現的突發事象，絕不能忽視它是於1910年代探索新日本固有建築様式潮流裡出現的的建築事件。但是，分離派建築運動並非單純只是繼承1910年代的討論而已，在那裡引出斷絕線，往下一個階段發展，換言之，就是大步向前接受現代建築運動建築的分離派建築會成立事件。於1910年代討論的基本框架是「是意匠，還是結構？」「是裝飾？還是實用？」的二元論，有各自的主張，與各自的擁護，或是這兩者的折衷。但是分離派建築會並非要在辯證法上去解消那樣的二元論，並且在摸索新的建築創作之根據上與過去所有的的討論都不相同。
於建築界意識性地使用「創作」的用語，開始自分離派建築會。過去因為明治時期國民樣式的要求，而使用了「創造」這個用詞，但是「創作」的用詞意味根據個人的「藝術意欲」之制作意義。這時候也教養主義經典性存在的阿部次郎（1883-19590）《三太郎日記》（大正3年刊）為學生們愛讀的時代。有不少學生學習世界各地的種種學藝，注視理想的自己，一步一步累積研鑽的成果。作為這樣的時代的風雲兒的分離派建築會成員，為了創作而賭上自己的所有，去拓展自己的學識，磨練自己的感性，致力於陶冶自己的人格。經過這樣的過程注力於新作品的「創作」。
話雖如此，只憑著人格或是自己的藝術意欲，是無法進行創作的。他們探尋創作的根據，找尋各方面的可能性線索。如〈田園〉、〈彫刻〉、〈構成〉。對這些課題有很高的興趣。在其背景，存在混雜著都市化的發展與大衆消費社會的出現、關東大震災與鋼筋混凝土造建築的普及、藝術思潮從表現主義轉變為合理主義等等的複雜關係。出現於時代的轉換期的分離派建築會之作品與思想，可以用這三個課題為縱線，及以時代背景為橫線以交織出錯綜複雜體。本書就是用全部8個章節32篇的論考來解開這個縦横交錯的絲線。

課程概述:
See https://tingwenlan.notion.site/Galaxy-Astrophysics-2026-7a67551e317c4839829057354c7db8fa for the latest version

How do galaxies form and evolve in the Universe? This question has puzzled astronomers since the discovery of galaxies over 100 years ago, and addressing it remains one of the central research directions in modern astronomy.

In this course, we will discuss our current understanding of galaxies from both observational and theoretical perspectives. The course is divided into two parts. The first part focuses on the observational properties of galaxies. We will discuss how the physical properties of galaxies are estimated and/or inferred from observational datasets. We will cover all major components, including stars, supermassive black holes, the interstellar medium (ISM), the circumgalactic and intergalactic medium (CGM/IGM), dark matter halos, and the connections among these components. We will also introduce the techniques astronomers use to study galaxy properties.

Building on this overview of observed galaxy properties, the second part of the course focuses on the theoretical aspects of galaxy evolution. We will discuss the formation and evolution of dark matter halos within which galaxies form and evolve. We will then cover key baryonic processes—such as gas cooling, inflows, and feedback—that are thought to play crucial roles in driving galaxy evolution. We will examine how these processes are implemented in numerical simulations and summarize our current theoretical understanding of galaxy evolution. Finally, we will discuss future directions in the study of galaxy evolution.

(1) This course is designed for graduate students and advanced undergrad students who are conducting astronomical research or plan to conduct astronomical research. Therefore,  background knowledge of physics and astronomy is expected. 

(2) This course is offered in English. 

(3) This course requires reading papers and oral presentations. 

(4) Programming abilities (such as Python) are expected.

課程概述:
The interstellar medium is matter and radiation permeating the vast space between stars. This course will introduce the physical processes in the interstellar medium that play a critical role in the life cycles of stars and galaxies.

Lectures will be given in English.

Part 1: Fundamentals

Week 1: Statistical Mechanics in the ISM
- thermodynamic equilibrium
- Saha equation
- collisional rates

Week 2: Recombination and photoionization
- collisional ionization equilibrium
- photoionization equilibrium

Week 3: Energy level of atoms and molecules
- electronic, vibrational, rotational transition
- selection rules

Week 4: Absorption, spontaneous and stimulated emission
- oscillator strength
- line profile and line broadening
- equation of radiative transfer

Week 5: Collisional excitation
- 21 cm line
- two-level system
- critical density
- the curve of growth


Part 2: The multi-phase ISM

Week 6: Neutral atomic gas
- heating and cooling processes
- thermal instability
- two-phase model

Week 7: Interstellar dust
- extinction and scattering
- thermal emission

Week 8: HII regions
- thermal balance
- the Strömgren sphere
- line diagnostics

Week 9: Fully ionized hot gas
- cooling processes
- the circumgalactic medium

Week 10: Molecular hydrogen
- dust and gas formation channels
- photo-dissociation and shielding
- correlation with star formation

Week 11: Molecular clouds: observation
- CO as a tracer for H2
- CO rotational lines
- radiation trapping

Week 12: Star formation
- Jeans instability
- ambipolar diffusion
- Kennicut-Schmidt relation

Week 13: Stellar feedback
- photoionization
- supernova blastwave
- stellar wind

Week 14: Turbulence
- energy spectrum
- Larson's relation
- star formation efficiency

Week 15: Putting it all together: gas cycle in the ISM

Week 16: Final oral exam
課程目標:
Understand the physical properties of the diffuse gas and dust in the interstellar space.

Understand how multi-wavelength observational signatures originate from different phases of the ISM.

Understand the lifecycle of gas, metals, and dust and their role in galaxy formation and evolution.
課程要求: Prerequisites: basic knowledge of E&M, thermodynamics, quantum physics, and fluid dynamics will be helpful but not required.

課程整體目標

•	Homework A：觀測坪實地量測（Field-based） 
1.	將觀測坪中的儀器分為五種不同設備（溫、濕、風、雨量筒、遙測） 
2.	學生兩人一組，每週輪流負責其中一種設備，記錄資料並描述當下環境條件 
3.	比較不同設備（架設在理想位置與不理想位置）的量測結果，討論為何會有差異？ 是天氣？是環境？還是儀器？

4.	加分作業：請學生到觀測站址實際觀察記錄環境，討論哪些地方可能造成量測誤差？有哪些「看起來合理但其實有問題」的設計？

0.	Overview

1.	Introduction – The atmospheric continuum, physical dimensions and units, scale analysis, the fundamental forces, non-inertial reference frames and apparent forces, and structure of the static atmosphere.

2.	The basic conservation laws – Total differential, the vertical form of the momentum equation in rotating coordinates, the component equations in spherical coordinates, scale analysis of the equation of motion, the continuity equation, the thermodynamic energy equation, thermodynamics of the dry atmosphere.

3.	Elementary application of the basic equations – The basic equation in isobaric coordinates, balanced flow, trajectories, streamlines, streamfunction, the thermal wind, vertical motion, and surface pressure tendency.

4.	Circulation and vorticity – The circulation theorem, vorticity, potential vorticity, the vorticity equation, the barotropic (Rossby) potential vorticity equation, the baroclinic (Ertel) potential vorticity equation.	

6.	Synoptic-scale motions I: Quasi-geostrophic analysis – The observed structure of extratropical circulations, the quasi-geostrophic approximation, quasi-geostrophic prediction, diagnosis of vertical motion, idealised model of a baroclinic disturbance.

8.	The planetary boundary layer – Atmospheric turbulence, turbulent kinetic energy, planetary boundary layer momentum equations, secondary circulations and spin-down.

力基礎。此外，為了增進同學之瞭解並提高學習興趣，常以實際所發
生的天氣現象或天氣系統為討論對象。

動力學；接著即進入天氣學的主體部份，包括有氣團、鋒面與鋒生、
氣旋與旋生、反氣旋以及高波波動。然後，在準地轉理論基礎上，探
討天氣系統之形成、發展、運動以及如何進行天氣診斷分析。最後，
則是介紹熱帶大氣特性與熱帶氣旋(颱風)之結構、形成、發展和運動。

課程概述:
This course explores how and why Earth’s climate comes about. We will not only introduce what a
typical weather condition is over each region on Earth, but also how and why climate, statistic of
weather, varies geographically and even temporally throughout the earth’s history. To understand how
climate system works, this course discuss concepts of radiative transfer, fluid dynamics, and
thermodynamics, with an emphasis of providing an overview of the energy balances that are
important for shaping and maintaining the vertical and meridional temperature profile, which is
crucial for climate.

In a companioning course, general circulation, a in depth discussion of angular momentum balance
and its role in controlling winds will be offered.
課程目標:
There are three main goals for this course:
(1) Essential puzzles: have a solid theoretical understanding of the mechanisms shaping the climate
system, including radiative convective equilibrium, meridional energy and momentum transports
(2) Big picture: understand the key factors influencing various mechanisms, apply the theories to the
real world and understand their limitations
(3) Little details: 
a. have a vague memories on various factors influencing climate in different
regions, so that you know where to look (when the key factors cannot explain a specific
phenomenon you aim to understand) in the future. 
b. Go through exercises in the textbook
carefully, making sure your understanding of the concept is thorough and memorable

To reach these goals, we design a series of activities for you to experience how scientists use models,
observations, and theory to understand past and current climate and make predictions for future
climate.
課程要求:
The course is designed to serve as a capstone project for Seniors majoring Atmospheric Sciences.  Students are expected to bring all of the related knowledge and skills into the course.
Students from other departments with strong motivations are more than welcome to talk to the instructor before taking the course.

這些故事將著重的主題包括大氣的組成和結構、輻射和能量平衡、天氣系統、空氣汙染、大氣中的基礎化學反應、溫室氣體以及氣候變遷。這是一門對所有對科學感興趣的學生開放的入門級課程。授課形式包括兩小時的講課與討論，以及由學生提問為主導的一小時討論時間。
課程目標: 學生將透過引人入勝的故事學習關於大氣環境的種種物理化學過程，並在課程結束後，對探討大氣環境更有動力與啟發的深層議題。

課程概述:
在地球科學的數值模擬與分析中，資料同化為一個重要的領域。藉由基於統計理論的資料同化技術，我們可使觀測資訊被客觀且最佳化地採用於數值模式中，得到模式分析場，對初始化模式預報相當重要。
本課程介紹資料同化的概念，研習地球科學領域中數種常用的資料同化方法，包括變分資料同化以及系集卡爾曼濾波器等方法。亦將介紹本領域中最新的進展，以及其在作業數值天氣預報中的實作與應用。
課程目標:
Introduction
Mathematical review
Empirical analysis schemes
Optimal interpolation
Kalman filter & extended Kalman filter
3D-Var
4D-Var
Ensemble Kalman Filter
Hybrid data assimilation
Verification & diagnostics
Operational NWP & reanalysis
NWP & data assimilation at CWA
Recent advancements in AI/ML approaches to data assimilation
Project: Development of data assimilation systems with a toy model
課程要求: There will be mid-term exam(s) and one term project. For the project, students will be asked to write computer code (using any programing language) performing data assimilation experiments with a toy model. The project work is important for students to gain deep understanding of data assimilation theory by real practice, instead of just reading course materials and deriving equations. Students will also be asked to develop their own scientific questions with their data assimilation code and present the results in the class.

The special short course will focus on fundamentals of tropical cyclones and use them to explain tropical cyclone genesis, motion, structure and intensity changes, balanced dynamics, waves, boundary layer, and climate aspect. We will also briefly discuss modeling and prediction of tropical cyclones with advanced numerical models. Key references (book chapters and review papers) will be given in the class. The lectures will be given in PowerPoint presentations. A handout lecture note summarizing each topic will be distributed just before each class.

課程概述: 企業管理這門課，是管理領域的入門課程，其目的在提供各種進階管理課程之基礎，因此對於管理相關科系的學生而言，企業管理是進入管理知識殿堂的重要基礎課程之一，透過這門課，學生得以一窺各種管理理論之堂奧。
課程目標:
總括而言，這門課的內容在回答以下兩大問題：
1. 企業是什麼？企業的功能是什麼？在當代全球化動態競爭的環境下，企業如何經營與競爭？
2. 管理是什麼？經理人在做些什麼？面對複雜多元的組織環境，如何把管理的工作做好，以達成組織的目標？
本課程即是上述兩個議題的融合。我們希望同學在這門課中，能夠學習到這兩大方面的知識，為往後更進階的相關管理課程的學習做好準備。而同學也必須明白，在實務上，企業與管理、競爭與組織、如何管理「事」、如何領導「人」，這些眾多議題都是環環相扣，彼此關聯的。

We will also motivate students to ask questions and engage them to participate in the discussion.

課程概述: Understanding the molecular structures of biomolecules and proteins, in particular, is essential for our understanding of how biological functions, such as gene transcription regulation, enzyme reactions, signal transductions, host-pathogen recognitions, are achieved. Since the DNA double helix structure reported by Watson and Crick, and the first protein structure reported by Kendrew and Perutz in the 50’s, the field of Structural Biology has witnessed several quantum jumps thanks to the breakthroughs in molecular cloning, genomic sequencing, and artificial intelligence (AI). Three-dimensional structures of complex biomolecules at atomic resolutions can be determined by X-ray crystallography, nuclear magnetic resonance (NMR) spectroscopy, cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) single particle analysis, and AI-based protein structure predictions and designs, such as AlphaFold and RosettaFold, the winners of the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry. Recent advances in native mass spectrometry (MS) further provide complementary details regarding complex assemblies, post-translational modifications and ligand binding under native environments. This course aims to provide a comprehensive overview about the basic principles and applications of X-ray crystallography, NMR spectroscopy, cryo-EM and MS in Structural Biology, and how the structural insights can be used to better understand how Biology works. Emphasis will be put on the introduction of visualization softwares to generate graphical images and animations of protein structures to glean atomic insights into the mechanisms underlying their biological functions.
課程目標: The goal of this course is to ensure that every graduate student in the IBS program, including both master's and Ph.D. candidates, irrespective of their background in chemistry or biology, acquires comprehensive and up-to-date knowledge in biological chemistry. This includes gaining a solid understanding of both chemical biology and structural biochemistry, equipping students with the foundational and advanced concepts necessary for research in these fields. By the end of the course, students will be proficient in the latest developments and techniques in structural biology, ready to apply this knowledge to their research and professional work.

課程概述: 近年冷凍電子顯微鏡（cryo-EM）的快速發展，使我們能夠在細胞中觀察到過去未曾看見的原位超微結構，為生命科學研究開啟了新的契機。本課程將介紹冷凍電子顯微鏡（cryo-EM）與冷凍電子斷層掃描（cryo-ET）的基本原理，並探討近期的重要研究成果。透過這些案例，學生將學習如何設計與執行實驗，以及如何分析與解讀所得結果。

課程概述:
在當前快速變遷的工作世界中，生成式人工智慧（GenAI）最深遠的影響，將體現在其如何被應用來重新構想與設計整個組織架構。這一深層次的變革預期將以去中心化與分散式的方式展開，由遍佈經濟各個角落的「創新者」與「創業家」共同推動。在這個前所未有的時代，創新與創業的能力顯得比以往任何時候都更加關鍵。

本課程旨在協助學生全面理解 GenAI 時代中所蘊含的創新與創業機遇，並掌握應對未知挑戰所必需的思維轉型。課程前半段將從探討 GenAI 在創新創業領域所帶來的挑戰切入，特別關注這項劃時代的通用技術所引發的顛覆性影響與不確定性，並系統性地討論相應的應對策略。當學生初步認識到 GenAI 時代的創新與創業藍圖後，自然會對未來產業中的創新趨勢與機遇產生疑問：在 GenAI 驅動的變革浪潮中，我們該如何抓住新興的發展契機？

未來的科技與產業發展將以「提供以人為本的前瞻性問題解決方案」為核心。過去，傳統產業或學科僅被視為構成解決方案的技術元件；而未來，跨領域的創新以及應對未知的能力將成為競爭力的重要指標。

這裡所謂的「未知」包含兩個層面：一方面，GenAI 的發展充滿不確定性；另一方面，人類能夠超越 GenAI 的關鍵在於我們應對未知挑戰的能力。創業家必須運用逆向思維來探索全新的需求與機遇，並藉由跨領域創新能力，打造真正具有顛覆性的商業模式。基於此，下半學期的課程將以跨領域創新為主軸，全面介紹涵蓋網際安全、大數據、人工智慧、物聯網、生物科技、醫療器材、APP 及元宇宙等領域的新創動態。

課名: 次世代電子病歷與智慧醫療生態系
開課系所: 醫學工程學系 / 生醫電子與資訊學研究所
課程概述:
課程單元與內容重點：
第一部分的內容介紹了醫院資訊系統的主要模組及其功能，涵蓋電子病歷系統（EMR）、影像儲存與傳輸系統（PACS）、醫院資訊系統（HIS）、實驗室資訊系統（LIS）、藥品管理系統及臨床決策支持系統（CDSS）。EMR 的重點在於病患資料的全面管理，包括病歷、檢查紀錄及治療計劃，而 PACS 主要用於醫學影像的存取與共享，確保醫師能迅速取得患者的影像資料。HIS 的核心功能則是涵蓋病人掛號、預約安排、財務處理和行政管理等。此部分還探討了全球領先的醫療系統供應商，如 Epic Systems、Cerner、Allscripts 和 Meditech，這些系統在互操作性、資訊安全及使用者界面上的設計特點被詳細描述。
第二部分專注於醫院內的作業流程，特別是急診系統的運作。以台大醫院的急診系統為例，展示了如何高效處理病人掛號、分診、進行必要的檢查及診斷。此段還涵蓋了住院與門診系統的運作，描述了從病人入院管理到床位分配、病情紀錄與出院流程的細節。此部分邀請了台大醫院資訊室主任分享他在開發與應用醫療資訊系統過程中的實際挑戰與心得。
第三部分聚焦於實驗室資料標準化與其應用，深入介紹了 LOINC 的起源與其在全球實驗室資料交換中的重要性。此部分解釋了如何在 LIS 中運用 LOINC 碼，以確保不同系統之間的資料互操作性，並安排學生進行實作練習，嘗試 LOINC 編碼以加深理解。此外，邀請實驗室專家進行實務分享，闡述如何在日常工作中應用 LOINC。
第四部分講解醫學名詞的標準化與文本轉換，深入分析了 SNOMED CT 的結構與其在 EMR 中提升標準化的應用。此段落包含實作練習，學習如何將醫療文本轉換為 SNOMED CT 編碼，並展示如何利用大語言模型進行自動轉換。學生將運用特定轉換工具來熟悉編碼的功能與局限性。
第五部分專注於國際藥物編碼與台灣的推展策略，介紹了 RxNorm 的背景及其在國際與台灣的應用，並說明其與 ATC、健保碼的對應關係。此部分還提供使用國家開發工具的 RxNorm 編碼練習，讓學生親自體驗藥物資訊標準化的過程。
第六部分深入討論臨床品質管理與規則語言，介紹 CQL 和 CDS Hooks 的概念及其在臨床決策中的重要性。學生將學習如何撰寫 CQL 規則，並模擬應用 CDS Hook，體會其實際操作。期中報告要求學生展示所撰寫的 CQL 規則與應用於模擬情境中的 CDS Hook。
第七部分探討進階課題，總結課程內容。詳細介紹了 SMART on FHIR 的架構，並帶領學生進行相關實作。此外，討論台灣 Core IG 與資料治理原則，並將其與國際法規如 GDPR 和 HIPAA 進行比較。此段落還著重於電子病歷系統的資安驅動技術與資料共享中的倫理議題。最後，分享台灣智慧醫療生態系統的發展，闡述三大醫療 AI 中心的設立及其對未來的影響。課程總結旨在提供學生全面的醫療資訊系統知識與實作能力，使其能應用於不同醫療場景，掌握最新的技術與標準化趨勢。

上課時間: 週五上午10:20-12:30

課程目標:
醫院的資訊系統，這可以說是整個醫院運作的神經中樞。過去，各家醫院通常自行開發適合自身需求的系統，這些系統在各自的運作中表現良好。然而，在智慧醫療時代，由於各家系統不相容，導致無法形成足夠的大數據來訓練人工智慧。此外，病患的資料無法在不同系統間互通，且無法在不同平台使用統一的醫療應用程式，難以形成應用程式的生態系。
資訊系統的碎片化，不僅影響了最後的競爭力，還嚴重損害了病人連續性照護的安全。美國自2016年開始推動《21世紀治療法案》，經過五年的研究，終於在2022年推出相關法規。這些法規要求，所有電子病歷系統必須符合並使用FHIR格式的標準，且所有應用程式必須遵循SMART on FHIR統一的標準。
這項法律自2022年實施，若電子病歷系統未使用該標準，即屬違法。此法案的推動下，帶來了大規模的變革，促使全球醫院系統開始更新並採用新的技術潮流。
這門課程的目標是介紹電子病歷的基本原理、主要組成部分，FHIR格式的相關應用，與SMART on FHIR標準。課程將結合台灣正在推動的次世代電子病歷相關政策及具體計畫內容，作為教育材料，讓學生了解台灣目前的最新發展，並培養具備運用此系統架構能力的人才，進而掌握當代醫療應用程式生態系的監控與發展。
課程要求:
這堂課程的評分標準包含幾個重要部分，首先是課堂出席。出席率將直接影響最終成績，確保學生全程參與課堂的討論和學習活動是至關重要的，這有助於提升互動學習效果。其次，期中和期末報告是課程的重要評估項目，學生需以小組形式進行報告，主題由授課老師指定，涵蓋醫院資訊系統的關鍵議題。報告需體現出內容的深度與完整性，展示學生對相關領域的深入研究和分析。此外，報告中需包括針對主題的系統設計或簡單程式實作，來展示學生的實務應用能力。每位小組成員需清楚說明其在報告中的具體工作和貢獻，這樣可以幫助授課老師掌握各成員的參與和貢獻度，確保個人成績的公平分配。
團隊合作成績是評分的一部分，小組的整體表現會影響每位組員的成績，但授課老師也會根據個人貢獻進行必要的調整，保持評分的公平性。這種評分方式有助於鼓勵學生積極參與並共同努力完成報告。
課程採用實體與線上混合教學模式，根據授課老師的具體安排進行。授課老師有特殊安排或需要邀請國際講者時，課程將以線上形式進行。此外，部分客座講者因交通或其他因素，可能選擇線上授課。這種安排提供學生接觸國際專家的機會，擴展學習視野。
實作課程將全程以實體進行，以確保學生能獲得即時的技術指導和支持。這樣的實作設計旨在讓學生有充分的實務訓練，增強他們對課程內容的理解和應用能力。整體而言，這種混合式教學模式在保持高質量學習體驗的同時，提供了靈活性以應對不同情況和需求。
