課程目標:
課程中，將透過實作行動體驗與同儕社群的交流支援系統，探討以下三個問題作為主軸：

【我是誰？】

「我是誰？」向來是個難以回答的大哉問。在設計人生中，我們會透過「同理」與「定義」兩個設計思考步驟，藉由回顧過往生命經驗，透過日常習慣、興趣嗜好、人際關係、自我認同、價值觀與信念等等不同的面向，來幫助我們看清自己身處何處、要走向何方及如何前進。

【我要做什麼？】

更認識自己是誰之後，我們會透過設計思考中的「發想」步驟，結合對自己了解的收斂，透過與多元背景組成的社群的激盪，發展出對未來規劃的不同想像，建立對於人生不同可能性的開放心態。

【我要怎麼做？】

許多時候，思考並不足夠，我們更需要實際行動。在課程中，我們會以設計思考中「原型」的精神，試著以最小可行性的思維，幫助自己降低嘗試新事物的門檻，踏出行動的第一步，並在失敗中學習與優化，在「測試」中迭代自己的計劃，並試圖展開下一次行動。

【什麼是設計你的人生？】
設計人生，是一套奠基在設計思考架構上，用以人為本的思維角度出發，將「自己」作為「使用者」與 「設計師」來看待自己人生的一套方法。
在不同的工具、活動與體驗中，與同伴 ( Partner )、導師 ( Mentor ) 、引導員 ( Facilitator ) 三個角色共同投入設計人生歷程，包含同理自己、定義自己的價值觀與需求、發想對於未來的可能性、制定簡易但足夠體驗的行動方案、快速測試並驗證對於自己的猜測與認識，最後進一步修正自己的未來生活想像，並以此流程不斷循環，漸漸建立屬於個人的生活與工作樣貌。


【設計人生的引導員在做什麼？】
設計人生的引導員主要投入在課程與活動帶領、組別引導討論、一對一個人引導，在不同的形式中，協助學員進行自我探索、釐清個人困境、建立行動方案、勾勒對於未來的想像，讓學員可以先從被動的帶領釐清，漸漸建立主動覺察的能力，並陪伴學員在不斷行動與反思的過程中，調整適合自己的生活步調與想像。
課程目標:
【情境梳理】
與學員互動時，從引導員與學員的對話中，逐漸組織其故事之完整邏輯與情境脈絡。

【重擬問題】
自梳理後之情境，釐清表層癥結點，並透過引導技巧，協助學員逐步探詢深層原因，進一步找到學員真正的問題與需求。

【解決方案】
挑出適合的工具，幫助學員建立解決問題的行動方案，並將目標拆解成更小行動，降低學員的行動門檻。

【需求對焦】
釐清學員的需求，挑選出合適的學習點，以體驗的方式讓學員接受新的觀點並做出改變的行動。

【課程設計】
1. 深究不同工具、活動與概念的核心學習點與核心體驗。
2. 能建立單堂的活動或課程。
3. 進一步嘗試建立長期且前後連貫的帶狀課程架構。

【團隊合作】
創造好的團隊文化，能用好的溝通方式與引導員夥伴協作完成課程與活動。

【有意識的觀察】
觀察課程學員之間、學員與引導員之間、組別之間等，不同角色的互動關係與模式，加速修正與迭代課程、活動帶領。

【什麼是設計思考教練】
「設計思考教練」透過設計思考的方法與心態，協助團隊遇到挑戰時辨識當下最重要的問題，並引導團隊在問題中持續探索與共創。總歸一句話，設計思考教練總是思考著：「我們如何能在模糊挑戰下，協助團隊持續展開行動來突破困境與達成目標？」

開課系所: 創新設計學院 / 領導學程
課程概述:
課程助教 蘇星瑋 b10310015@ntu.edu.tw

當代社會問題趨向複雜而難解,牽涉的行動者和利害關係人多元,包涵著各種互動而交織的社會系統和政治系統,各種解決辦法都會改變部分並連動引發另一些改變,甚至影響到全球人類生存,因此,未來人才必須跨越既有思維模式。大學教育除了過去的多學科(interdisciplinary)模式,保持原學科獨特求知的模式,整合舊知識來解決共通的問題,例如輔系、雙修和通識課程等方式,更興趣了跨學科(transdisciplinary)模式,以真實生活世界中的主題,或是學生應習得的技能為目標,跨越學科界限而設計教學過程。 台大創新設計學院在2015年創立後,致力於培養學生跨領域的創新設計與創造實作之能力,也看到台大學生在學習和實踐的過程中,每個人會走出不同的模樣!
本課程希望為有興趣走出舒適圈、剛開始嘗試跨領域的你,提供一個開箱體驗的機會,幫你打開跨域學習的眼界,看見生活中無所不在的跨域元素。 課程內容將會涵括的要素包括本學院跨領域學習課程、創新領域學位學程、創新創業學程、領導學程等。此外還有設計思考入門體驗,提供跨域方法論,讓同學們進行微型跨域活動。聆聽走在前面的師生分享,經由個人反思和團體激盪,邁出跨域實作的第一步。在為期四週的課程裡環顧四周,為自己的跨域學習找到各種可能的方向,解放雙腿,大步跨出,開始屬於自己的探索旅程!
課程目標:
修課學生在完成本課程後，預期能夠：
1. 認識跨域學習的重要及資源：認識跨領域與跨學科思維的差異，體會其在當代複雜議題中的應用價值，並認識D-School提供的跨域相關學習資源。
2. 認識設計思考：認識設計思考，並體驗如何運用設計思考流程進行問題洞察、構思與提出初步解決方案。
3. 展現跨域合作素養與溝通：具備與不同背景同儕共同討論、分工與協作的經驗，並能在團隊中有效貢獻。
4. 激發創造力與實踐動能：勇於突破既有框架，嘗試新的學習與實踐方式，開展個人跨域探索的可能方向。
課程要求:
1. 本課採取密集課程方式,在學期第二到五週的週二上午進行,每週三小時,第四週的週二晚上6-9點進行專題討論，第五週課長四小時(9-13點)。選課前請評估你的學期時間規劃。
2. 課程以體驗與反思為主要學習方式,學生須充分參與課堂討論及實作。
3. 跨出趣行動:學習了跨域的方法後,在生活中找到跨域的實際案例,藉由個人參與投入的過程,分析其中的跨域特質。例如:看展覽,看電影,研究產品,分析商業模式,了解網紅經濟...等,基本上,能給出一套說法解釋它為何及如何跨域的事都可以。課程最後每人繳交一張海報(電子檔),呈現個人在跨出趣行動中得到的跨域新視界與學習所得。

課名: 包皮與割禮：文化、醫學與權力的跨域探究
課程概述:
包皮（prepuce）是人類身體的微小構造，其存在與功能跨越了生物學、宗教、文化與政治的邊界，成為歷史上最具爭議的身體部位之一。從古埃及的宗教儀式，到現代醫學中的衛生論述，再到人權與身體自主的全球辯論，包皮與割禮的議題揭示了人類社會如何在身體上刻畫信仰、身份、權力與道德。
本課程以跨學科視角透過四大主題(醫療與科技、性別與殖民、宗教與倫理、割禮無國界)與八大領域(醫學生理、組織再造、公共衛生、歷史文化研究、宗教學、性別認同、人類學與倫理學) 深入淺出，環繞「身體自主權」與「文化多樣性」的張力，交叉檢視文化、醫學與權力在包皮與割禮中的相互關係，引導學生以批判性與同理心思考「誰擁有身體」這一核心問題。學生將學習包皮的生理特性、生物權力與身體政治，理解各文化中對割禮的象徵意義，並深入分析其在宗教儀式、身體人類學、種族脈絡、後殖民歷史、法律人權、國際公共衛生政策與當代性別的角色。
本課程一個學期共二學分，每週上課二小時，藉由 16 週循序漸進的課程安排及不同專業背景的大學老師及一位業界人士(特別演講)，帶領修課同學由生物、醫學、科技、人文、宗教及倫理的面相了解包皮以及衍伸的種種醫學與社會議題。
課程將以出席率和個人期末上台口頭及五個短影音報告作為最大評分依據。

本課程開放10名加選名額，欲加選的同學請於二月二十五日下午四點五十九分五十九秒前將短於一分鐘的影片檔案電郵寄送賴育宏老師信箱（laiyuhung@ntu.edu.tw)。影片需自我介紹並說明選課動機。 長於一分鐘的影片將不受理。成功入圍加選名單的同學將在三月四日下午五點前以電子郵件通知確認，並隨確認信附上加選授權碼。
課程目標:
教學目標：環繞「身體自主權」與「文化多樣性」的核心主軸，促進跨域的包皮與割禮相關知識、對話與思辦
‧	認識包皮的生理與演化功能。
 ‧	分析醫學史上對包皮的病理化與現代公共衛生政策的爭議。
‧	說明割禮在不同宗教與文化中的起源與象徵意涵。
‧	探究割禮在生物權力、身體政治與人類學、種族脈絡、後殖民歷史、與當代性別的角色。 
‧	評估有關割禮的倫理、法律與人權議題，包括兒童身體同意、自主權，不可逆性與兒童權利與宗教自由的平衡。

學生學習成效：以「包皮與割禮」作為核心分析對象，整合及表述多面向的科學及人文議題，體現通識教育「以具體案例培養跨域思辨能力」之核心精神。

開課系所: 無授課對象 / 經濟學系 / 國際企業學系 / 財務金融學系 / 會計學系 / 社會科學院院學士學位
課程概述: This course offers a comprehensive exploration of macroeconomic issues, encompassing the analysis of aggregate output, employment, unemployment, economic growth, the monetary system, interest rates, inflation, international trade, and exchange rate. 課程概述: This course provides an introduction to a broad range of concepts, theories, and analytical techniques of macroeconomics. It focuses on the analysis of how an economy as a whole operates and performs, with introduction of analytic tools and models used to explore national income, economic growth, unemployment, price indices, consumption, inflation, saving, investment, international trade, and international finance.
課程目標:
1.	Be able to describe the major realms of modern macroeconomics, and how to define a related economic question
2.	Learn the concept of national income and GDP
3.	Be able to operate basic macroeconomic models to analyze elements of national income
4.	Learn the concepts of inequality and poverty
5.	Acquire an understanding on economic growth and sustained growth
6.	Learn about the roles of market size, labor division, technology advancement, and entrepreneurial management.
7.	Be able to derive equilibrium of macroeconomic models and analyze shocks
8.	Acquire an understanding of employment and unemployment of the market as a whole
9.	Learn about credit markets and banking system
10.	Learn about monetary system of an economy
11.	Be able to identify the features of macroeconomic fluctuations
12.	Be able to derive and operate international trade models 
13.	Acquire an understanding on open economy macroeconomics

o	Assignments (20%)
o	Midterm examination (40%)
o	Final examination (40%)

課程概述:
本課程系統性介紹現代總體經濟學的核心理論架構，重點在於理解經濟成長、跨期決策，以及總體波動的內在機制。課程首先從長期經濟成長出發，依序探討馬爾薩斯模型、Solow 成長模型，以及內生成長理論，說明人口、資本累積與技術進步如何共同決定經濟的長期發展趨勢。
在建立長期成長的理論基礎後，課程將轉向動態分析，介紹兩期（two-period）模型，著重於個體在跨期選擇下的消費、儲蓄與投資決策，並說明金融市場與利率如何影響資源在時間上的配置。此一架構亦作為後續動態總體模型的基礎。
最後，課程將進一步探討總體經濟波動，介紹景氣循環的基本理論，並分析生產力衝擊、不確定性與政策因素如何影響產出、就業與投資的短期動態表現。透過理論模型與經濟直覺的結合，本課程旨在培養學生對總體經濟現象的整體理解與分析能力。
課程目標:
1. 建立總體經濟學的核心理論基礎
使學生熟悉經濟成長理論、跨期選擇與總體波動等現代總體經濟學的基本分析架構，並理解其背後的經濟直覺。
2. 理解長期經濟成長的決定因素
透過馬爾薩斯模型、Solow 成長模型與內生成長理論，分析人口成長、資本累積與技術進步如何影響長期經濟表現。
3. 培養跨期決策的分析能力
運用兩期模型探討消費、儲蓄與投資決策，理解利率、金融市場與制度環境如何影響個體與總體層面的資源配置。
4. 分析總體經濟波動的來源與機制
說明生產力衝擊與其他總體衝擊如何透過動態機制影響產出、就業與投資，並培養學生解讀景氣循環的能力。
5. 強化理論模型與實際經濟現象的連結
引導學生將理論模型應用於理解現實世界的總體經濟議題，並提升其閱讀經濟文獻與進行經濟分析的能力。
課程要求:
1. 課前準備與課堂參與
學生應於課前完成指定閱讀，並積極參與課堂討論與課堂練習。
2. 課堂小考（兩次）
本課程將安排兩次課堂小考，以評量學生對核心理論模型與分析工具的理解與應用能力。小考內容以課堂講授之重點為主，包含模型推導、計算題與經濟直覺說明。
3. 期中考試
期中考將評量學生對經濟成長理論與跨期決策模型之理解與分析能力。
4. 期末考試
期末考將涵蓋全學期內容，特別著重於動態模型與景氣循環分析，評量學生整合理論與解釋總體經濟現象的能力。
5. 學術誠信
本課程嚴格遵守學術誠信原則。所有考試與小考須為學生個人獨立完成，若有違反學術誠信之行為，將依校方相關規定辦理。

課程概述:
This course introduces the foundational concepts of econometrics. Most importantly, we will cover the linear conditional expectation function and linear regression. Toward the end of the course, we will touch on the potential outcomes framework and provide a brief introduction to causal inference.

The primary goal of this course is for you to gain an in-depth understanding of linear regression.

While we emphasize basic concepts, econometrics is fundamentally a practical tool. A significant portion of the assignments will focus on practical applications. We adopt a hands-on approach, guiding you to explore and utilize relevant resources effectively. Think of this course as a workshop designed to build your data analysis skills within the field of econometrics.

Mastering these concepts requires considerable effort. As a guideline, plan to dedicate approximately three hours of study per week for each credit hour. This course carries 4 credits, so you should expect about 20 hours of weekly engagement. This includes two hours of in-class interaction, leaving 18 hours for independent study and assignments.

Each week, you will have access to 1–2 hours of pre-recorded lectures, complemented by 4 hours of practical exercises on DataCamp. Additionally, plan for approximately 4 hours of homework and supplementary reading each week.

課程概述:
這是兩學期課程的第一學期，但也可以單獨選。第一學期主要探討早期經濟史，並以此為基礎探討一些重要的經濟概念。課程首先簡要回顧農業革命和早期文明的興起，然後考察「軸心時代」（戰國時期和漢朝的中國、古希臘和羅馬、佛教印度以及絲綢之路）的世界經濟，之後進入中世紀經濟（唐宋時期的中國、伊斯蘭世界和歐洲）。接下來，我們將探討「大分流」現象，即歐洲經濟起飛並變得比亞洲更加富裕，最後我們將考察莫臥兒王朝和英屬印度、明清時期的中國以及德川幕府和明治維新時期的日本。在這些歷史講座中，我們會穿插一些關於重要主題的講座和討論。例如，掠奪和保護以及生產在解釋經濟成長中的重要性、不同類型自由的重要性、家庭結構和文化的影響、規模經濟的影響、學習的發生方式以及變革通常是自上而下還是自下而上等問題。上課方式是兩節課講課和中間一節課的討論（或專案實作環節）。
第二學期（也可以單獨修讀）將更探討1900年後的經濟史（主要集中在亞洲）。
Note: My first language is English.  Whenever the Chinese syllabus is unclear, please check the English syllabus.

------
由於選課人數眾多，不開放旁聽。課程內容紮實深刻，不甜也不涼，專門給關注心理健康與創傷的學生。
本課程提供的是框架與地圖，並非臨床心理治療。作為通識課程，提供的是概括式的思考框架，不會涉及個人議題。

------
2/23 第一週 14:30 開始上課。


在勞動經濟學，健康經濟，公共經濟學，甚至總體經濟學，近年開始探討惡性事件以及早期介入政策對於人的影響為何? 從警察暴力，大屠殺，種族隔離，校園槍擊，種族歧視，到早期治療與介入政策，經濟學家使用資料分析當事者在事件後的發展並衡量其人生影響。

創傷在此指的是在特定負面經驗下，超出個人當時可整合能力的內在心理痛苦，其影響在事件結束後仍持續存在，形塑人的情緒反應、行為模式與選擇。面對痛苦，最常見的生存策略就是壓抑和逃避痛苦的感受。這些適應性策略在特定情境中有效，但事過境遷後，甚至在安全的環境下，仍可能持續影響我們的反應與選擇。

韌性在此指的是從傷害中復原，以及在困難的處境下仍能保有希望的能力。生命總是苦樂相伴。我們無法避免惡性事件的發生，或是完全沒有任何痛苦的生活經驗，但如何從傷害中復原，接納並穿越生命中的苦難? 

命運，或者說未來，是由我們生命中一系列的選擇而形成。但我們的選擇受到過去生命經驗與環境的影響。如果沒有覺察到這些，未來往往是不斷重複的過去。因此覺察到尚未被處理的議題與傷痛，有助於我們理解自身的選擇並反思，進而能更清楚地回應自己此生真正的關切與承擔，以及與更大整體相連的方向，清晰我們的命運。

在面對生命的挑戰與選擇時，有兩個極端的框架。一邊是純粹的個人主義，認為自我是完全獨立的個人，選擇完全由個人的自由意志決定，而忽略了更大的系統性背景影響。另一邊是集體主義，認為個人的選擇都來自集體的影響，命運早已被決定。復原與韌性來自於中間的平衡。即理解到我們生命中的挑戰與困擾，不僅僅是個人的，同時也來自於更大的系統性問題，有一部分來自於我們成長的文化，社會，與制度。創傷與韌性，同時存在於個人與集體之中。因此，我們對自身的理解與治療，與背後更大的系統密不可分。

本課程主要使用人際神經生物學 Interpersonal Neurobiology (IPNB) ，內在家庭系統治療 Internal Family System Therapy (IFS)和祖先療癒 Ancestral Medicine (AM) 的框架 (簡稱為IIA) 來理解個人與社會集體的創傷，並提供療癒的地圖。課程會從個人的創傷與治療出發，進一步探討跨世代傳承的家族創傷，最後到社會文化與制度的集體創傷與韌性。

課程支持並尊重每位學生獨特的生命經驗，致力於提供一個多元平等，反性別歧視，反種族歧視，反對各種霸權主義 (例如男性至上，學歷至上等)，肯定LGBTQ，肯定每個人自我保護的防衛機制的空間。課程不建議學生揭露自身的創傷經驗，並以尊重個人界線與心理安全為教學原則。

覺察並處理過去的傷痛以及未解決的議題，可以幫助我們實現自身最佳可能的命運，活出最好的可能性。因此本課程協助探討哲學三問: 我為什麼活著？我應該怎樣活著？我如何能活出應該活出的生命？屬於A4哲學與道德思考領域。

課程從個人出發，協助察覺到我們的成長環境，社會文化，制度，例如父權主義，種族主義，性別歧視，升學主義等對我們造成什麼影響，以及如何從個人擴展到社會集體的治療與復原之路，屬於A5 公民意識與社會分析領域。

本課程同時包含了理論知識以及具體實踐的練習，歡迎對於心理健康，創傷與治療有強烈興趣的同學來修習。
課程目標:
本課程主要目標為培養學生對「創傷知情」與「療癒知情」的理解能力。

創傷知情指的是了解到創傷是什麼以及它的影響，日常生活中有哪些反應以及選擇是由於過去未解議題的影響等。在修習本課程後，期望學生能以創傷知情的角度理解自己與他人，進而降低以病理化或簡化的標籤來理解生命經驗與行為的傾向。

所謂療癒知情，指的是理解不同理論與實務框架中，如何思考創傷的復原、轉化與韌性，以及療癒歷程所涉及的核心原則與限制。修習本課程後，期望學生能理解，創傷的治療往往是一個長期，複雜，且沒有時間表的歷程，並能認識在個人與集體層次中，支持復原與韌性發展的可能條件。

本課程的目的是提供理解創傷與治療的框架與地圖。本課程並非臨床心理治療，亦無法取代專業心理治療或諮商服務。

課程概述:
This is a topics course on Neuroeconomics. According to Wikipedia, “neuroeconomics combines neuroscience, economics, and psychology to study how people make decisions. It looks at the role of the brain when we evaluate decisions, categorize risks and rewards, and interact with each other.” Together we will read a set of papers which would serve as an introduction to some of the fun themes in the field.

Each week we will discuss a paper in detail. A group of students will make a presentation weekly.  We will discuss the research question asked, the experimental design, the result, the interpretation of the result in the paper, and whether we as readers will run the experiment differently and whatever interests, excites or confuses us when reading the paper. In sum, this is a course where everyone gets to speak up a lot!

Because it is a topics course, our goal is not to be comprehensive. Each year we have a different focus. The topics of this year have yet to be decided. But likely we will focus on the following. Online communication has become prevalent during the COVID-19 pandemic. Physical social interactions are particularly missing. We would like to better understand the behavioral and psychological impact of this. Moreover, the pandemic may cause negative emotions such as fear and loneliness. It may even cause substance use.  This makes new safety learning or memory-modifications relevant. A detailed reading list will be provided at the first class meeting.
課程目標:
Our goal is to help students learn to speak up. In order to do that, students, in groups, have to present papers. When they are in the audience, they are encouraged to ask questions and join discussions.

Hence, we break the goal into two steps. Understanding a paper is the first step. Only with a thorough understanding can one present the paper and handle the questions. Being able to criticize it scientifically is the next. Only when one criticizes a paper scientifically will s/he start to see whether the results are convincing.

Hence, we try to create an atmosphere where students can feel easy to speak up, in order to learn to talk about science.

課程概述: This course will introduce several resource allocation problems including cooperative game theory, bankruptcy problems, cost-sharing problems and etc. Meanwhile, fair allocation mechanisms will be introduced for each class of resource allocation problems. This course studies allocation mechanisms from the axiomatic approach. The departure point of the approach is the properties of allocation mechanisms. These properties are formally stated as axioms and used to compare allocation mechanisms. The ultimate object of the approach is to trace out the boundary between those combinations that are compatible and those that are not, and when compatible, to give as explicit as possible a description of the family of allocation mechanisms satisfying them. The properties of allocation mechanisms often are motivated by several fairness or justice criteria. This course will introduce the criteria and explore their implications.
課程目標: The objective of this course is to examine and understand another perspective of individual behavior, except for competition, namely cooperation. What motivation and incentives bring people to work together? How to fairly divide the benefit or cost generated from cooperation when there are conflicts of interest among agents? Such questions will be answered during the lectures. Hopefully, students will build up a solid knowledge and foundation of cooperation microeconomic analysis and familiarity with logic arguments.

這門課帶你運用經濟學原理和市場設計的分析架構，從「內容 vs.平台」的關係出發，解析內容產業的經營邏輯，並討論新科技將如何重塑產業生態與內容樣貌。

我們所謂的「內容產業」，涵蓋了影視、出版、音樂、遊戲、社群、廣告、展演與沉浸式體驗等，也有人稱之為「娛樂及媒體產業」。因此，這門課適合對相關領域具有高度興趣的同學，以及願意以內容產業為例，深入研習最前沿的市場研究與產業分析方法的同學。課程內容除了馮老師講課，還包括個案討論和作業，會用到基本統計學、數據分析和問卷調查方法。

1. 新媒體導向：以 YouTube、Netflix、Webtoon、TikTok、Amazon 等國際平台平台做為主要研討案例，分析方法亦可套用到 Spotify、Steam、Podcast 等其他內容產業領域。

2. 實戰數據應用：部分作業取自真實產學合作案，並提供YouTube後台數據、Netflix觀看數據，與大型市場調查的原始數據，供同學練習。

3. 強烈科技元素：納入內容產業的數位轉型、數據轉型相關課題，討論新科技、大數據、演算法和AI，正如何重塑產業樣貌與媒體內容。當平台的經營者從媒體巨頭轉向科技巨頭，整個內容產業的競爭已成為一場科技競賽！

課程概述:
This course will survey empirical methods in labor economics. We will focus on recent advances in causal inference as well as their applications. The topics will include matching methods, difference-in-differences design, synthetic control, regression discontinuity design, instrumental variables, as well as machine learning techniques such as LASSO, random forests, and causal forests for estimating heterogeneous treatment effects. In addition, the course introduces students to working with geospatial data (GIS) and other emerging data sources beyond standard survey data. The applications in labor economics include AI and labor market, life-cycle labor supply, social insurance, labor demand, and tax incidence. 

Throughout the course, we place a strong emphasis on the practical implementation of these methods and on best practices in managing real-world data. Students will apply what they learn by writing a term paper, which must be typeset using LaTeX. By the end of the course, students should have built a solid foundation for conducting independent empirical research and for writing their theses.

課程概述:
In An Essay on the Principle of Population (1798), Thomas Malthus presented a pessimistic outlook on future population growth. However, with the global population doubling over the past 50 years and reaching 8.23 billion at the end of 2025, was Malthus truly wrong?

    To address this question, this course first examines global demographic transition patterns, investigating both general trends and specific country characteristics. Second, we will introduce core concepts of demographic transition, focusing on two pivotal factors: fertility and mortality. We will pay particular attention to the phenomenon of ultra-low fertility in East Asian countries. Specifically, we will discuss the interplay between Artificial Intelligence (AI) and fertility decisions, exploring how technological shifts might influence reproductive choices. Finally, the course will explore the causes of population aging and discuss potential policy responses.
課程目標: By the end of the semester, students will be able to: (1) Gain a comprehensive overview of global demographic transitions. (2) Grasp fundamental concepts in demographic economics. (3) Understand the links between demography and economics. (4) Identify the challenges posed by population aging and evaluate possible solutions.

(2)	Analyze the prevailing challenge in the existing association between CEO early life experience and CEO management styles literature,
(3)	Analyze the long-run effect of fetal origins hypothesis on socioeconomic and non-health outcomes,
(4)	Analyze the effect of pollution on investor behavioral bias and corporate policies,
(5)	Analyze the effect of CSR (or ESG) on stock performances and financing policies,
(6)	Analyze the effect of climate change risk and opportunities on stock performances and firm policies,
(7)	Analyze the effect of ESG lending and ESG equity,

On successful completion of this course, students will be able to:

(1) Critically evaluate empirical research in corporate finance;
(2) Compare policy implications of CO2 emission reduction for corporate policy; and
(3) Compare various asset pricing models of climate change risk exposures

課程概述:
The goal of this course is to familiarize students with empirical analysis in industrial organization (IO). Specifically, we will focus on estimating demand and market power using the approaches developed by New Empirical Industrial Organization (NEIO). The primary aim is to equip students with the tools and techniques needed for empirical research in IO, enabling them to pursue their own research projects in the future.

Traditionally, Industrial Organization examines the interactions of oligopolistic firms. For example, from an antitrust perspective, regulators need to access whether a proposed merger should be allowed. A crucial factor influencing firm interactions is consumers’ demand for differentiated products. One of the central theme in empirical Industrial Organization is estimating demand, particularly in differentiated-product markets. Specifically, we will introduce the Berry, Levinsohn, and Pakes (BLP) framework, a widely-used method for empirical demand estimation in differentiated markets. Using this framework, students will learn how to estimate demand, model market competition, and analyze issues such as price discrimination, competition of durable products, advertisement, and network effects. In addition, this course will briefly introduce the programming procedure required to implement these empirical methods.
課程目標:
By the end of the course, students will be equipped with the empirical tools to:
• Estimate demand in differentiated-product markets
• Analyze market power and competition
• Apply the BLP framework to various economic problems

課程概述:
This course examines the role of financial frictions in macroeconomic and monetary theory. Financial frictions arise from asymmetric information—such as adverse selection and moral hazard—as well as from limited enforcement. We study how these frictions constrain borrowing capacity and how fluctuations in collateral values can amplify and propagate exogenous shocks, generating volatility in aggregate economic activity and asset prices.
We then turn to empirical evidence on monetary transmission mechanisms, with particular emphasis on the credit channel and the risk-taking channel. In addition, we analyze models of bank runs arising from fragile bank balance sheets and asset fire sales. Finally, the course addresses the role of monetary policy and macroprudential regulation in mitigating business cycle fluctuations and safeguarding financial stability.

5. Monetary Policy and Financial Stability

課程概述:
本課程以邀請學界研究者進行專題演講為核心，旨在透過實際研究經驗的分享，協助學生理解經濟學研究的方法、思維與實務運作方式。課程將涵蓋不同研究領域與研究取向，讓學生從多元主題中觀察經濟學研究問題的形成、研究方法的選擇，以及理論與實證分析的實際應用。
透過講者的研究發表與經驗分享，學生將接觸經濟學研究在不同子領域中的具體操作，包括理論模型的建構、實證設計與資料分析，以及研究成果如何轉化為學術論文與政策討論。課程亦將引導學生學習如何閱讀與提問，培養對研究動機、方法選擇與研究貢獻的理解與批判能力。
整體而言，本課程著重於讓學生透過第一手的研究展示，理解經濟學研究的實際流程與學術社群的運作方式，並為未來從事研究、論文寫作或進階學習奠定基礎。
課程目標:
本課程之主要目標如下：
1. 理解經濟學研究的實際運作方式
透過邀請學界研究者進行專題演講，使學生了解經濟學研究從研究問題形成、方法選擇到研究成果發表的完整流程。
2. 熟悉多元研究方法與研究取向
藉由接觸不同研究領域與方法（理論、實證或混合取向），協助學生建立對經濟學研究方法多樣性的整體認識。
3. 培養學術聆聽與提問能力
訓練學生在研究發表場合中掌握研究動機、核心方法與主要貢獻，並提出具建設性的問題與評論。
4. 提升論文閱讀與批判性思考能力
引導學生評估研究設計與方法選擇的合理性，理解研究限制，並培養批判性思考與學術判斷能力。
5. 建立研究導向之學習與交流習慣
協助學生熟悉研討會（seminar）文化與學術社群運作方式，為未來從事研究、論文寫作或進階學習做好準備。
課程要求:
1. 出席與準時參與
本課程以專題演講與討論為主，學生須準時出席每次課程並全程參與。出席情形將作為課程評量之重要依據。
2. 課前準備
學生應於課前閱讀指定之講者論文或相關資料，並事先思考研究動機、研究方法與主要研究結果，以利課堂理解與討論。
3. 課堂參與與提問
學生需於演講與討論時間中積極參與，包含聆聽、提問與回應討論。課堂提問與討論表現將列入平時評量。
4. 課後反思與學習回饋
學生可能需於課後繳交簡短之學習反思或心得，整理講者研究內容與方法，作為學習成效評估之依據。

    另108課綱強調「探究與實作」，希望透過「專題探究實作，強化跨領域/學科的統整」。師資職前教育課程基準強調師資生須具備「探究與實作的設計與實施」之教師專業素養。探究過程中需查找與閱讀許多資料，但中學生常因閱讀與寫作能力不足，影響探究成效。又許多師資生在大學期間，未經歷探究過程，帶領中學生探究頗感辛苦。本課程遂以閱讀、寫作為工具，達成探究的目標。師資生不但要親身經歷探究過程，並據以設計閱讀融入現象本位跨學科的課程，引導學生進行現象本位的專題探究，以符合新課綱對教師的期待。
課程目標:
（一）培養自身讀寫能力
（二）透過小組探究學習，以發展溝通、問題解決的教師專業素養。
（三）閱讀融入現象本位學習，設計跨領域探究專題的課程、教學及評量。

課程概述:
本課程以中學數學課程之試教演練為主。每位學生選定兩個高中數學主題(一個主題要包含至少三堂課的份量)做深入研究，並針對此主題製作教案、設計評量，進行試教。這門課以四周為一個循環，每循環將探討兩位同學選擇的主題並最終進行試教。各周的課程活動如下:

第一周: 閱讀「十二年數學領域綱要」、「數學領域課程手冊」，與不同版本的課本，理解這主題內各概念、公式、應用間的邏輯關係。再把主題放在較大的脈絡下，整理它的先備知識、相關主題和引申內容。最後，做出一個「你認同的教學詮釋」，並回答以下問題: 
「這個主題想教會學生什麼數學概念？這個概念為什麼重要？它和甚麼主題有連結？」
「課本如何解釋、說明這個概念？有沒有其他方法？ 我會怎麼鋪陳這個主題?」
本周課堂中將決定本主題內要試教的單元。

第二周: 為主題制定課程大綱，並設計評量問題。
課程大綱: 負責同學為整個主題編寫至少三堂課(50分鐘一堂課)的課程大綱；大綱需確定每堂課涵蓋的概念和單元間如何銜接，並估計教學節奏和學生的認知負荷能力。負責同學在課堂中報告大綱。全班再為將試教的單元討論可能的教學過程，特別是激發動機的引言、實作活動(計算機)或生活應用。
設計評量問題: 非負責同學為試教單元提供教學用和考試用的題目(至少四題)，在課堂中報告討論。每個題目需標示「測什麼能力」，例如，概念理解、應用公式、計算能力或連結推理能力？

第三周: 負責同學提供一單元的完整教案，所有同學在課堂中針對該教案進行討論，給予建議。教案需預想學生可能出現的錯誤或迷思並設想如何回應。非負責同學尋找該單元的線上課程、教學影片或是坊間現有講義，介紹該教材的優缺點，並討論「如果我是這一單元的老師，我會在哪一部分使用這些教材？」

第四周: 試教，把教案付諸實際教學。每一單元包含 40 分鐘試教與 20分鐘回饋檢討。回應時請回答以下問題: 概念說明是否清楚？問題設計是否引出學生思考？ 是否引起學生的學習動機?
課程目標:
•  透過研讀課程綱要並比較不同版本之教科書內容，學生能理解並清楚說明特定主題的整體脈絡。
•  學生能獨立編寫以 50 分鐘為一單元之完整教案。
•  學生能依據試教主題，設計適切且具鑑別度的評量問題。
•  學生能分析與評估自己及他人教案的優缺點。
•  透過課堂中實際試教，學生能實踐教案。
•  藉由課堂中的討論，學生能對他人的試教提供具體、建設性的回饋，並檢視自身試教成果。
課程要求: 修過數學教材教法。

課名: 電資工程入門設計與實作
課程概述: 本課程旨在引導學生透過動手實作探索電機資訊領域，同時培養其主動學習及問題解決之跨域能力。有別於傳統單向講述的教學方式，本實作基石課程希望透過一系列引導式實驗與問題解決導向之實作專題，讓學生透過做中學，激發其主動學習動機，強化其運用電機資訊科技解決問題之能力，並提升跨領域整合能力。
課程目標:
一、引導電機系一年級學生透過對資通訊(ICT)相關專題探索與實作， 培養基本工程素養:
- 深入掌握問題/現象本質
- 具體定義問題
- 積極創新，解決問題
- 主動團隊溝通、合作
- 精實生動的科技報告

課程概述:
本課程將介紹半導體元件之基礎物理原理。課程首先從固體晶體結構與量子力學基本概念出發，說明其在固態系統中的應用。接著將介紹半導體於熱平衡狀態下的電子性質，並探討外加電場作用下之載子傳輸現象。接著，課程將介紹非平衡狀態下之載子動力學，包括過剩載子的產生、復合與傳輸機制。隨後，將說明核心半導體元件之基本原理，重點涵蓋 PN 接面理論、二極體之操作特性，以及金屬—半導體接觸特性。本課程培養學生對半導體物理之理解與分析能力，作為理解當代電子與光電元件之重要基礎。

課程內容：
1.固態晶體結構 (The Crystal Structure of Solids)
2.量子力學及固態量子理論概論 (Introduction to Quantum Mechanics and the Quantum Theory of Solids)
3.熱平衡半導體 (The Semiconductor in Equilibrium) 
4.載子傳輸現象 (Carrier Transport Phenomena) 
5.半導體非熱平衡過量載子 (Nonequilibrium Excess Carrier in Semiconductor) 
6.PN接合面及二極體 (The PN Junction Theory and Diode ) 
7.金屬半導體接觸及異質接合面(Metal Semiconductor Contacts)

課程主題如下:

主題I: 光電基本功
(a) 從本徵值觀點看Maxwell Eq.光學各項異性與偏振
(b) 從動量守恆觀點看介面反射譜、臨界角與複數介電質產生之相位與應用 
(c) 從Jones Matrix法分析平面波傳播與光迴路(波片…)問題、干涉與應用

(g)	從簡諧振子看介電係數建模(Drude Model)與修正, n&k反射光譜逆向分析

(i)	Schrodinger, Poisson Eq. 之本徵問題與有限差分法求解，自洽計算

(k)	低能隙共價鍵半導體之光學躍遷與吸收/輻射譜

(n)	基於動量守恆之量子芯片，糾纏光子源與應用

電工實驗（通信專題）是針對電機系三、四年級學生所開設的實作課程。此課程的主要部分包含：
（一）實際操作數位無線通訊主要步驟。
（二）以最新論文為例，評析無線通訊之應用及實驗。

（一）	實際操作數位無線通訊主要步驟
【Week 1 – Week 6：個人MATLAB實驗】
課程學期前六週會使用MATLAB產生以及處理無線通訊訊號，並模擬傳輸及接收。課程涵蓋digital modulation and demodulation, up-sampling and down-sampling, filtering, frequency conversion, synchronization, channel estimation, 以及orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (OFDM)。同學在前六週使用MATLAB所產生的訊號，以及訊號處理的程序，將在後續課程結合USRP進行實際無線傳輸與接收。

【Week 7 – Week 12：小組USRP實驗】
課程七至十二週會進入USRP操作，觀察常見硬體缺陷對無線通訊的影響，並且傳輸與接收無線訊號。此部分實驗為2-3人一組，同學可自行分組。進入USRP實驗後，課程會有額外由助教帶領的實驗時段，預計會選擇週間的傍晚，實際時段會依修課同學可以參與的時間一起決定。

（二）	無線通訊應用及實驗評析——以最新論文為例
本學期前十二周期間，將透過四次論文評析，從而了解無線通訊網路領域的最新應用，並深入評析其中實驗設計及實驗結果。論文主要從無線領域的頂級會議中選擇，論文會與課程主題相關或是介紹獨特應用。希望透過論文中多樣化的主題，拓展同學們對通信領域的認識，加深基礎操作與應用之間的連結，有助於同學們期末專題的選擇。

課程概述:
[Course description]

Control is the action of causing a system variable to approach some desired value. It is also a fundamental and universal problem-solving approach in many traditional and interdisciplinary fields.

A control system, in a very general sense, is a system with an (reference) input that can be applied per the desired value and an output from which how well the system variable matches to the desired value (e.g., errors) can be determined. It can be found in daily life, almost all engineering disciplines, and even biological and social studies. For examples, bicycle riding involves a control system comprising of a bicycle and a rider, with inputs and outputs associated with the desired attitude, speed, and direction of the bicycle. Temperature control systems have applications in household, automobile, aerospace, office, factory, and agriculture environments. Motion control systems are critical to factory automation and precision instruments, such as industrial robots, atomic-force microscopes, and step-and-scan photolithography exposure systems. Many modern cameras equip with autofocus and vibration compensation systems to minimize image blur. Many kinds of circuits such as phase lock loops, operational amplifiers, and voltage regulators rely on control to ensure their functions and performance. A living body is a complex control system where many critical variables such as heartbeat rate, blood pressure, and body temperature are regulated constantly for health. Central banks of most countries around the world set interest rates as a way to control inflation.

This undergraduate course is designed for junior and senior (3rd/4th yr.) students to apprehend basic modeling, simulation, analysis, and design techniques for control systems. It intends to cover the fundamentals of “classical control” that primarily focuses on frequency domain feedback control approaches for single-input-single-output systems. When time permits, some essential elements in modern-day control engineering such as state-space techniques will be covered.
課程目標:
[Course goals]
Basic:
- Awareness of the strength and the importance of control systems, especially the effectiveness of feedback
- Ability of deriving dynamic models and simulating dynamic responses
- Ability of analyzing and designing feedback controllers for linear SISO systems in the frequency domain using root locus and frequency response techniques
Bonus:
- Awareness of some advanced control topics (e.g., state-space methods, digital control, and nonlinear systems)
- Development of technical writing skills in English
課程要求:
[Prerequisites]
Linear algebra, ordinary differential equations, Laplace transforms, fundamental circuit and mechanics analysis -- which should have been well covered by several freshman and sophomore (1st/2nd yr.) courses in most electrical and mechanical engineering curriculums. Prior exposure to the analysis of signals and systems will be beneficial but not absolutely required.

課程概述:
This is an introductory course on computer networks, largely the Internet. The course is designed for undergraduate students who are interested in the science and engineering aspects of the Internet. The goal is two-fold: to communicate the technical essence and to foster development skill.

We will take the top-down approach this semester. Following a (hopefully) brief overview, the lectures will go right into the Internet applications most of us are familiar with, e.g., the WWW and the HTTP protocol that is supporting the operation of WWW. HTTP there is referred to as an Application layer protocol. The intention is to go 3-4 weeks per layer, digging in to the low-level details one layer at a time, e.g., the TCP protocol running at the Transport layer, and the BGP routing running at the Network layer. When time permits, we shall look into the Ethernet protocol running at the Link Layer.

Communication of knowledge is often more effective when it's put into use. Eying also the job prospective, the course features a series of programming assignments (PAs) and accompanying videos to lead you into the world of network and web programming with Go, a programming language adopted widely by the major Internet companies, e.g., Google and Facebook, for server-side implementations.
課程目標:
1. Overviewing the existence and the components of the Internet
2. Examining the mechanisms running in various layers
3. Understanding the nature of the problems these mechanisms are trying to solve
4. Developing system-level coding skill
課程要求:
1. Introduction to Computer Programming (C-like or Python knowledge required)
2. Introduction to Computers (fundamental computer system knowledge required)
3. Data Structure and Programming Languages (preferred)

課程概述:
本專題研究旨在引導學生將電磁學（Electromagnetics)理論應用於下一代 AI 伺服器之核心硬體架構——GPU/TPU 高速互連系統。隨著 NVIDIA NVLink 與 UALink 協定邁向單通道 200Gbps (PAM4) 的極限速率，傳統連接器與線纜已成為系統效能的瓶頸。本課程將結合產業實務需求，深入探討高速連接器、主動式銅纜 (ACC) 及被動式銅纜 (PCC) 的技術特徵。學生將學習如何處理高頻下的趨膚效應（Skin Effect）、電介質損耗、串擾（Crosstalk）及阻抗不連續性等物理挑戰。課程內容涵蓋：
高頻模型建立： 使用 ANSYS HFSS 等電磁模擬軟體進行 3D 結構建模。
訊號完整性分析： 探討插入損耗（Insertion Loss）、反射損耗（Return Loss）與眼圖（Eye Diagram）之優化。
前瞻互連技術： 研討 224G 世代下銅導線的物理極限與矽光子（Silicon Photonics）技術的競爭與協作關係。
課程目標:
1. 理論與實務對接： 能夠運用電磁學理論解釋高速連接器在 $20\text{ GHz}$ 以上高頻環境中的電氣行為，特別是阻抗匹配與傳輸線效應。
2. 模擬工具應用： 熟練掌握業界主流的電磁波模擬工具（如 HFSS 或 CST），針對宏致電子開發之高速連接器外型進行訊號完整性（SI）模擬。
3. 關鍵參數分析： 具備解讀 S 參數（S-parameters）的能力，並能針對模擬結果提出結構優化建議（如針腳排列、遮蔽結構設計），以降低串擾與共振點。
4. 掌握產業趨勢： 深入了解 AI 伺服器架構中主動式銅纜（ACC）與矽光子（SiPh）的技術差異，並能評估不同材料（低損耗 PCB、極細同軸線）對訊號品質的影響。
5. 解決方案開發： 針對 6G 與次世代 AI 運算需求，設計並驗證具備低延遲與高熱穩定性的連接方案，模擬真實產業中研發工程師的解決問題流程。

課程概述:
本課程著重於生醫工程領域中常用之生理訊號量測、訊號處理與應用開發，旨在培養學生具備跨領域的工程實務能力與醫療健康科技應用視野。課程內容涵蓋 EEG（腦電圖）、ECG（心電圖）、EMG（肌電圖）、血氧量測、非侵入式血糖監測等多種生醫感測技術，並介紹穿戴式裝置、智慧醫療與腦機介面（BCI）等新興應用。

課程採分組實驗與專題實作相結合的方式，學生將從基本儀器與量測原理出發，學習生醫電子系統的設計、實作與資料分析，並進行創新應用的期末專題開發。透過課程訓練，學生不僅能建立生醫訊號量測與分析的專業基礎，亦能培養團隊協作、問題解決與跨領域創新之能力。
課程目標:
培養生醫電資工程與科學領域之專業人才，推動新興醫療與健康科技應用。

訓練學生熟悉生醫電子量測工具與方法，具備跨領域實作能力。

鞏固學生在硬體、軟體與資料分析上的綜合技能。

培養獨立研究與創新思考能力，能發掘、分析並解決生醫工程相關問題。

本課程分為兩個階段：

　實驗二：生醫信號量測電路之分析與設計

This course studies basic principles of optimal control.
Target students include those interested in the areas of
optimization and control of various dynamic systems

socioeconomic systems and biological systems.

We will explore linear optimal control theory
from an engineering viewpoint,
with step-by-step explanations
that show clearly how to make practical use of the material.
The lectures will include:

The linear regulators/trackers.
The Hamilton-Jacobi equation.
(B)
The engineering properties of the regulator:
degree of stability.,
phase and gain margin,
tolerance of time delay,
effect of nonlinearities,
asymptotic properties,
various sensitivity problems.
(C)
State estimation and robust controller design
using state-estimate feedback.

課程概述:
Formal methods represent an important research field in computer science where techniques with mathematical rigor are studied for the specification, design, analysis, and validation of computing systems. This course will cover formal methods for program analysis, especially those in the field of software model checking: Given a program and a specification, automatically decide whether the program satisfies the specification or not.

The model-checking algorithms we will introduce in this course include:

- Abstract interpretation
- Symbolic execution
- k-Induction
- Predicate abstraction
- Trace abstraction
- Interpolation-based approaches 

Compared to software testing, software model checking can prove the correctness of a program with mathematical rigor. Software model checking is rooted in a solid theoretical foundation, requires advanced software engineering for tool implementation, and has profound impact on both academia and industry: The inventors of model checking won the 2007 Turing Award, and leading software companies, such as Meta and Amazon, use formal methods to assure the quality of their products.

**IMPORTANT**: This course does not follow the mapping from point grades to letter grades provided by NTU.
課程目標:
After finishing this course, students are expected to:

- Be familiar with the mathematical foundation of formal methods
- Understand state-of-the-art algorithms for software model checking
- Independently conduct a research project on formal methods

課程概述:
Database management systems (DBMS) are fundamental to modern society, playing a critical role in science, engineering, business, and beyond. With the explosion of data volume and complexity, coupled with advancements in processing techniques driven by big data, data science, and machine learning, understanding databases has become more crucial and fascinating than ever. 

This course, "Database Management Systems: From SQL to NoSQL," offers a comprehensive exploration of both the theoretical underpinnings and practical applications of DBMS. We'll begin by establishing a solid foundation in database modeling, which serves as the bedrock for effective database programming and architectural design. Students will gain hands-on experience with both SQL and NoSQL database programming paradigms, delving into the intricacies of DBMS architectures to develop a deep understanding of database processing and management. Beyond traditional systems, we will explore cutting-edge topics, including the exciting intersection of Large Language Models (LLMs) and databases, and the role of knowledge graphs in representing and querying complex relationships. Recent developments we will also cover include vector databases (essential for efficient similarity search and retrieval in LLM applications) and graph databases (particularly suited for managing and querying complex relationships in knowledge graphs). 

While SQL programming is an important part of the course, its primary focus is not SQL training. Instead, this course is ideal for students aspiring to become software architects, to pursue research or practical work in database systems, or to seek a robust understanding of database principles to enhance their studies in related data-centric fields such as data science, data mining, deep learning, and the increasingly critical area of database security and privacy.

The final implementation-oriented project by the students is an integral part of this course.  If you are interested to take this course, please be reminded to reserve enough time toward the end of the semester for the completion of the project.
課程目標:
1. Understand fundamental database concepts and the role of DBMS.
2. Develop proficiency in data modeling and schema design.
3. Learn the fundamentals of SQL and NoSQL database programming, providing a foundation for continued learning and mastery. 
4. Analyze DBMS architectures to understand their design and functionality.
5. Develop the ability to quickly learn and grasp new database technologies, including their data models, languages, and architectures.
6. Design and implement a final project that modify, augment, or build DBMS functionalities.

課程概述:
大家好！我是主授這門課的李宏毅。在《機器學習》這門課中，我們會用一個學期的時間，帶大家掌握我認為「現在就必須會、未來也真的用得上」的人工智慧前沿核心技術。人工智慧發展非常快，所以課程內容每年都會更新，今年也不例外。

今年最不一樣的地方是：人工智慧不只會「說」，也開始會「做」了。你可能已經在生活或研究中用到各式各樣的人工智慧工具與助理，它們正在把 AI 從聊天框裡帶到真實工作流程中。接下來你身邊會出現越來越多 AI Agent，幫你查資料、寫程式、跑實驗、整理文件，甚至協助你學習與研究，你會更直接地感受到，AI是一個能夠和你一起完成任務的夥伴。

而這些 AI Agent 背後真正的核心，就是生成式 AI 模型，尤其是大型語言模型。本學期我們會從 AI Agent 的視角切入，帶你看懂它們背後的核心原理。更重要的是，未來做模型開發，很少會從零開始訓練一個全新模型；更多時候，你要做的是站在已經具備通用能力的基礎模型上，讓它變得更強、更可靠、更符合你的任務需求。因此，今年課程的重點會放在「如何影響與調整模型行為」，教你如何強化特定能力、降低不想要的行為、讓模型更穩定地完成你指定的目標。

課程概述:
本課程為一門以實作為核心（practicum-based）的進階網路安全課程，旨在引導學生於虛擬化環境中，實際建構企業級網路架構，並透過開源工具模擬各類網路與主機攻擊情境，進而設計與實作對應之防禦機制。

課程採用 learning-by-doing 教學模式，依循 SEED（Security Education）專案之教學理念，讓學生在受控的虛擬機（VM）環境中，從攻擊者視角理解駭客技術，再轉換至防禦者角色，建立完整的網路攻防思維。全學期規劃約 14 個實驗（labs），涵蓋網路安全、Web 安全、主機安全、逆向工程、漏洞利用與密碼學等主題
課程目標:
修畢本課程後，學生在「特定條件下（VM 與實驗環境）」，應能「有效且正確地完成指定資安任務」，具體學習目標如下：

1. 能明確界定網路與系統之安全需求，並從竊聽（Eavesdropping）、身分驗證（Authentication）、完整性（Integrity）與可用性（Availability）四大面向進行分析。

2. 能設計具備實務可行性的企業網路安全架構，並說明其防護原理與限制。

3. 能辨識常見網路協定與系統實作中的安全弱點，理解其成因與可能風險。

4. 能實際操作開源資安工具，重現多種攻擊情境（如掃描、嗅探、Web 攻擊、漏洞利用等）。

5. 能設計、設定並建置防禦機制（如防火牆、VPN 與系統強化設定），並評估其在真實企業環境中的適用性與效能 。

課程概述:
As the sizes and functionalities of software keep on growing, non-trivial software projects have spent more than half of their budget in testing and debugging. For Taiwan's high-tech industry, the situtaion is even worse since most software team managers and engineers do not think that they should spend money in software testing. Such a mentality rooted from Taiwan's industrial strength in OEM and ODM business but is now hurting Taiwan's effort in brand business. With the know-how in requirement engineering and system testing, Taiwan has no hope in making a successful international brand in the high-tech industry.

Software security is a highly visible and fast-growing sector of software testing.  Not only the government has promoted and enforced security regulations, most companies are willing to invest in software security.
課程目標:
The course aims at teaching the students the background theory of software quality assurance (QA) and letting them play with advanced testing and security-checking tools from academia and industry.  In the long-term, we anticipate to produce skillful professionals in software testing business for Taiwan's high-tech industry that can do the following.

1. Knowing the fundamentals and resources in software testing
2. Utilizing the research results from academia
3. Deploying software testing technology to various companies.
4. Understanding the basic concepts and skills in security checking.

課程概述:
課程概述：
1.基本分子生物實驗的操作,包含細菌培養,DNA分離,電泳分析以及PCR. 
2.基因晶片備製過程學習 
3.細胞培養及RNA的提取 
4.總基因體學前處理流程
5.Real-time RT PCR
7.利用軟體進行結果之分析判讀以及推論實驗結果在生物上的意義
課程目標: 本課程旨在落實分子生物學與基因體學的實務操作。透過 DNA/RNA 萃取、PCR 與 Sanger 定序，銜接次世代定序與總體基因體學前處理；並結合生物資訊分析軟體，使學生具備實驗操作及數據解讀的能力。

課程概述: 本課程之目的為介紹與討論超音波在醫學上的應用、並實際參與實作演練。課程包含理論教授講演、實作演練實驗、以及設計實作專題。理論教授講演中包括介紹診斷超音波之成像原理、治療超音波應用、新興醫用超音波技術、臨床上的應用及挑戰、探頭製造以及工業界的新發展。實作演練實驗包含超音波發射、超音波接收、訊號分析、以及波束合成。實作專題將進行分組專題實作。課程第一周(退選截止前)將說明課程內容包含超音波自測實驗。參與本課程之學生可能將成為受測者，自行收取生理資訊，並作為未來研究資料。
課程目標:
1.	認識醫用超音波在醫學上之應用範疇。
2.	認識診斷超音波之成像原理、並能實際以電子電路實作觀察其物理及生物現象。
3.	認識治療超音波之治療原理、並能實際以電子電路實作觀察其物理及生物現象。
課程要求:
理論課程內容: 
1. Introduction to Ultrasound B mode imaging
2. Ultrasound physics
3. Ultrasound Transducers and beamforming
4. Ultrasound B mode instrumentation
5. Ultrasound Properties, limitations and artefacts
6. Principles of Doppler ultrasound
7. Ultrasound Quality assurance and safety
8. 3D ultrasound
9. Ultrasound Elastography
10. High-Intensity Focused Ultrasound
11. MR-Guided Transcranial Focused Ultrasound
12. Focused Ultrasound Field Simulation
分組專題實作: 
Lab 1. Interface design 
Lab 2. Interface design and signal processing
Lab 3. Pulse/echo structure
Lab 4. Pulse/echo integration
Lab 5. Ultrasound special project

課程概述: This course is an interdisciplinary subject divided into two main parts. The first half of the semester covers the biological background knowledge of cetaceans, such as classification, geographic distribution, morphological adaptations, evolution, life history, feeding habits, social structure, and communication intelligence. It also explores the past, present, and future of the relationship between humans and the ocean, the development and historical context of marine conservation, and delves into the concepts and ideologies of marine conservation. Furthermore, it provides an introduction to the concepts of conservation biology, learning its main theories and methods, and discusses how to implement marine conservation from various perspectives, including ecological, economic, and humanistic aspects. The second half of the semester introduces important issues in cetacean conservation, such as whaling, fisheries conflicts, the development of whale watching, stranding response, dolphin captivity, and marine protected areas.
課程目標: The aim of this course is to enable more students to understand cetaceans and their habitats, as well as the role of humans in relation to the ocean and marine life. Through the weekly discussions, students will have the opportunity to listen to others' perspectives, engage in personal reflection, organize and express their own opinions, and explore their subjective consciousness to understand themselves. It is hoped that this will lead students to delve into the issues existing between cetacean ecological conservation and human activity conflicts. Ultimately, after students have absorbed sufficient knowledge and deeply considered issues related to cetacean conservation, they are expected to share their creativity and ideas through a final report with their classmates. The goal is to plant the seeds of cetacean conservation in the students' minds, hoping that more individuals will join in caring for and promoting the conservation of cetaceans and the ocean.
課程要求:
There is a discussion session every week. 課程概述: Networks in ecology encompass almost anything that can be represented by a set of points joined by edges. For example, a food web represents the feeding relationships within a community, which underpins the structure of material and energy flows among organisms and, in turn, fosters biodiversity and ecological functions. This course consists of weekly two-hour lectures, covering fundamental concepts about ecological networks of various forms, as well as the relevant theories, quantitative and simulation techniques, implications, and applications. While the emphasis is on general concepts, case studies will also be introduced and discussed, supplemented with recent key studies.
課程目標: From the course, students are expected to comprehend fundamental concepts in Network Ecology, as well as relevant empirical and theoretical research methods. In particular, they should learn the ways of doing simple network analysis, making interpretation of network properties at different levels of organisation, and become familiar with contextualising recent publications in the field.
課程要求: Students should have taken General Biology and Ecology (both required). Possessing basic calculus and/or linear algebra understanding will be an advantage for comprehending this course, as the course covers some fundamental mathematics of network dynamics. The in-course practice may include hand-on network analyses, thus it would also be an advantage if the students can bring their laptop to the course, with R language installed.

課程概述: 蘭科植物（Orchidaceae）是世界上物種多樣性最豐富且最具魅力的植物之一，擁有極高的生態學、園藝學和經濟學價值。然而，由於棲息地破壞、非法採集和氣候變遷等因素，蘭科植物的許多物種正面臨著生存危機。這門課程旨在介紹蘭科植物的生態學、生物學、以及全球保育現狀，並探討相關的保育策略和技術。

課程概述:
在全球生物多樣性快速流失的時代，必須透過高效率的方式，蒐集大範圍、長時間的資料，作為瞭解現況、探討原因、合理預測、檢視保育政策與行動的主要資料來源，才趕得上生物多樣性流失的速度。幸好，同時網路通訊與社群網絡快速發展、智慧型行動裝置的普及，使公民科學成為生物多樣性保育的重要主工具，同時也累積大量的觀察紀錄與資料。

開課系所: 生態學與演化生物學研究所
課程概述: 本生物學課程旨在探討生物體及其與環境之間的相互作用。核心內容涵蓋細胞結構、遺傳學、演化、生態學與生理學，幫助學生理解生命的基本運作機制與多樣性。本課程亦探討基因工程、氣候變遷與疾病預防等當代議題，突顯生物學在因應全球性挑戰中的重要性。透過理論知識與實務技能的整合，本課程為學生未來進階學習或投身科學、醫療與生物科技等相關領域奠定基礎，並培養其對自然世界的好奇心。
課程目標:
1. 了解生命系統的核心組成與基本運作機制 
2. 理解生物體結構與功能之間的關係 
3. 認識生物與環境之間的交互作用及其生態意義 
4. 理解生物演化在形塑生物多樣性中的角色 
5. 認知生物學知識與人類社會、健康及環境議題之關聯

課程概述:
資(通)訊科技被視為繼蒸汽機、電力之後人類文明最重要的技術革命。它開創了個人電腦、網際網路、電子商務、行動應用等無數的新興產業，影響人類在政治、經濟、社會的所有活動構面。進入2020年代，這場數位轉型出現了質變的加速點──人工智慧，特別是生成式AI（Generative AI）。從語言模型、影像生成到AI Agent，AI不再只是自動化或輔助分析工具，而逐漸成為能夠參與決策、重塑工作流程、甚至影響組織分工與專業角色定位的「通用能力層」。《經濟學人》與麥肯錫等機構皆指出，生成式AI將為全球經濟每年創造數兆美元的新增價值；對企業而言，無法有效掌握此一技術浪潮將面臨嚴峻的生存挑戰。
在此背景下，本課程聚焦於新興資訊科技與 AI 應用，系統性分析其對企業經營所帶來的衝擊、機會與風險，並引導學員思考企業在不同發展階段下，應如何進行策略選擇、能力布局與治理設計。受限於授課時數，課程將涵蓋但不限於以下主題：隱私保護與資料治理、歐盟GDPR的合規挑戰、資訊安全與管理、人工智慧、生成式AI與AI代理人趨勢、機器人技術的商業化發展、社群商務與網紅經濟、智慧物流與供應鏈韌性、Web3與區塊鏈、以及從AR/VR走向空間運算（Spatial Computing）的沈浸式體驗等。
本課程強調應用與管理視角，而非技術實作細節，特別適合非資訊科技背景、但必須面對AI與數位轉型決策的高階經理人與企業領導者。部分概念與案例學員或許並不陌生，但課程的價值不在於「介紹新名詞」，而在於透過案例分析與課堂討論，協助學員建立一套能夠判斷：哪些科技值得投入、何時投入、以及如何與既有組織、流程與整體策略有效結合。

Information and communication technologies (ICT) are widely regarded as the most significant technological revolution in human civilization since the steam engine and electricity. They have given rise to countless emerging industries—including personal computers, the Internet, e-commerce, and mobile applications—and have reshaped virtually every dimension of human activity across political, economic, and social domains. Entering the 2020s, this wave of digital transformation has reached an inflection point marked by a qualitative acceleration: Artificial Intelligence, particularly Generative AI. From large language models and image generation to AI agents, AI is no longer merely a tool for automation or analytical support. Instead, it is increasingly becoming a general-purpose capability layer that can participate in decision-making, redesign workflows, and even reshape organizational structures and professional roles. Institutions such as The Economist and McKinsey have noted that generative AI could create trillions of dollars in additional global economic value annually; for firms, failure to effectively harness this technological wave poses a severe threat to long-term survival.

Against this backdrop, this course focuses on emerging information technologies and AI applications, providing a systematic analysis of their impacts, opportunities, and risks for enterprise management. It guides participants to think critically about how firms at different stages of development should make strategic choices, build capabilities, and design appropriate governance mechanisms. Given time constraints, the course covers—though is not limited to—the following topics: privacy protection and data governance; compliance challenges under the EU’s GDPR; information security and management; artificial intelligence, generative AI, and trends in AI agents; the commercialization of robotics; social commerce and the influencer economy; smart logistics and supply chain resilience; Web3 and blockchain; and immersive experiences evolving from AR/VR toward spatial computing.
The course emphasizes an application-oriented and managerial perspective rather than technical implementation details. It is particularly suited for senior managers and business leaders without formal IT backgrounds who nonetheless must confront decisions related to AI and digital transformation. While some concepts and cases may be familiar, the value of the course does not lie in introducing new buzzwords. Instead, through case analysis and classroom discussion, it helps participants develop a practical decision framework for determining which technologies are worth investing in, when to invest, and how to effectively integrate them with existing organizations, processes, and overall corporate strategy.

課程概述:
This course will meet weekly in a formal seminar format. Each week, a leading scientist will present his or her ongoing research (approximately 50 min, but can be longer). After each presentation, a Q&A session will be held.

Students take this course on a pass/fail basis. This course has no exams, and thus the grade is solely determined by the attendance. Two or more absences will result in an F (fail). Students who must miss a seminar may consult with the course instructor prior to the absence, but it is unlikely that an absence is excused. A tardiness of 10 min or more is treated as an absence.

In addition to the attendance, students are required to submit a report immediately after each seminar. Forms are distributed prior to a seminar. Students must write the evaluation/critique of a seminar. A report that is too rough/vague (including blank report) should not be submitted.
課程目標:
- To learn cutting edge research conducted (mostly) in Taiwan
- To experience how scientific information is transmitted (the 50-min presentation style is one of the main modes of scientific presentation)
- To learn how to gain most out of seminars
- To develop an own idea about what a good seminar is

補充說明: 

為何有 “科學研究計畫管理這門課? 

摘自 “昆蟲電子報" 19 期 (2009/5/31) 

科學研究計畫管理 - You have to learn how to learn 這是我大約一個月前由席德尼 布雷納 (Sydney Brenner, 2002年諾貝爾生醫獎得主) 的訪談中所學到的句子。我非常喜歡這句話，也在各個不同的場合分享給同學。然而，沒想到當我受邀為「不可不修的一堂課」撰稿時，這句話竟然成為我的「布雷納障礙」。因為，布雷納的本意正是鼓勵年輕的學子擺脫被動的課堂學習，勇於嘗試各種管道擷取新知；坦白來說，在他的眼中，真的「沒有不可不修的一堂課」！然而，如果要由我的開課清單中挑一門課推薦給同學，無疑地，「科學研究計畫管理」(Project Management for Laboratory Scientists) 是我的首選。

 大約三年前，在劍橋大學 (University of Cambridge) 南極研究中心工作的 Charles Cook 博士受聘至系上進行基因親緣遺傳分析以及短期講學。在他成行前，我告訴他台大素有自由之學風，因此他的授課內容與主題完全由其自訂。因為我當時已有一段時間沒有和這位老同事聯絡，不知他在研究之餘，又在劍橋大學取得 MBA 學位。當他告訴我要講授「科學研究計畫管理」時，我的確相當震撼；然而，「尊重自由學風」大話已出，只能故做鎮定，靜觀其變。令人欣慰的是，Cook 博士深入淺出的教學方式以及實用豐富的內容，在當時吸引滿座之同學 (含本系與其他學系的學生)，踴躍發言聲與歡笑聲不時由中非一樓大教室傳出。迄今，我仍深深懷念那一年的初夏！ 

隨著時光飛逝，到了兩年前的夏天，我得知 Cook 博士無法再次來台授課的消息，隨之憂鬱了起來。面臨停開這門課與否，著實令我陷入長考：「停開」的確是最簡單之方式，然而也是最不負責任之作法；「續開」的確可讓同學對研究工作之進行有所助益，但我實在無法「clone (複製) Chuck (Cook博士之暱稱)」。就在天人交戰之際，我無意間由莊榮輝教授的網站發現了「科學之路」(The Art of Scientific Investigation) 這本書的中譯本。當「科學之路」這四個字映入眼簾時，我的焦慮頓時飛散，並毅然決然的在暑假中詳研這本書，佐以原文版，完成教材之製作。因此在過去的四個學期，「科學之路」已成為「科學研究計畫管理」的教科書。雖然書名看起來有些哲學，出版年代也早在 1950 年初期，然而作者 Willian I. Beveridge 以其深厚的科學研究功力與洞見，使得這本書不僅在當時深受矚目與歡迎，其觀點迄今仍擲地有聲，切中追求優質科學研究之要點。 

我非常喜歡上這門課，因為我喜歡「科學之路」這本書，自己也行在「科學之路」。這門課不是教學生如何發表高點數的論文，也不是傳授申請研究計畫的竅門。這門課主要針對已經有些研究室經驗的大學部與碩、博士班學生，面對一個研究計畫，應如何從無到有進行規劃與執行。非常湊巧的是，我發現 Beveridge 的「科學之路」正是最佳的藍圖：從序言之「科學家與偵探」就直指科學研究計畫之進行需具備對線索鍥而不捨之決心與敏銳的蒐證能力 (我通常都會延請一位真正的辦案高手現身說法！)；接著「準備工作」、「實驗」、「機遇」、「假設」…，到最後的「戰略與戰術」、「科學家」等章節，很完整的說明了從事研究計畫會遭遇之挑戰、應有的態度以及解決之道。 

雖然選這門課的同學人數以及歡笑聲已不若 Chuck 開課時之盛況，然而同學們認真地參與討論，真誠地分享作業心得，還有眼中對科學研究露出不再恐懼的微光，都是鼓勵我每學期很樂意地走進課堂，一遍又一遍述說 Beveridge 的論點與解析當代科學研究趨勢的最大動力。行筆至此，我不禁又想到了 Brenner 講過的 "You have to learn how to learn" 這句話。我想「科學研究計畫管理」應該是為了具備這個能力所開的課。歡迎各位同學選修，課堂見！

課程概述:
The course consists of two main components: Experimental Design and Data Analysis. The Experimental Design section follows the textbook (https://x.gd/xbmz9), while the Data Analysis component focuses on the maximum likelihood method and introduces additional statistical techniques. Computer simulations are used to enhance an intuitive understanding of statistical concepts. Programming skills are emphasized to enable flexible model construction, allowing students to develop statistical models tailored to their data rather than relying solely on conventional models.

Although the course title includes the word 'ecology,' this is a general course on experimental design and data analysis. Students from all disciplines are welcome to enroll. While many of the examples discussed in class may relate to ecology, no prior knowledge of or interest in ecology is necessary.

The computer language R (http://www.r-project.org/) is used throughout the course. No prior programming experience is required.

Students are expected to have completed at least one semester of statistics (e.g., familiarity with Student’s t-test) before enrolling in this course.

Students must bring a portable computer with R installed to every class, except for the first class on February 26. Students who do not have a portable computer may contact the instructor regarding in-class borrowing, subject to computer availability.
課程目標: Students completing this course will understand how typical statistical tests, such as null hypothesis significance testing, work; be able to program in R; become familiar with common statistical models, including generalized linear and mixed models; and build their own statistical models when conventional models are not appropriate.

課程概述:
1. 解析基因功能之科技發展日新月異，對遺傳機制之理解已拓展至基因體學 (genomics)、個體生物學 (organismal biology)、基因行為學 (behavioral genetics) 之層次。盱衡現有之「分子生物學 (Molecular Biology)」課程，因著重講述「中心信條 (central dogma)」之運作法則，在有限的時數內，較難詳細闡明基因科技之運用及其演進。有鑑於此，在「分子遺傳學 (Molecular Genetics)」這個課程，希冀同學們能習得更多遺傳物質之傳遞機制，以及與時俱進之分子遺傳科技新知。

2. 有別「分子生物學」課程，新增重點涵蓋：(1) 基因體 (genome) 與轉錄組 (transcriptome) 序列解析；(2) 傳統與現代遺傳工程科技之演進；(3) DNA 修補原理及其應用；(4) 跳躍子 (transposable elements) 運轉機制及其衍生科技；(5) 發育遺傳學；(6) 基因行為學；(7) 昆蟲分子遺傳科技運用。

3. 課程內容與上學期的「分子生物學」課程不重複，但相輔相成。

4. 三小時授課安排：二小時「快樂授課」＋一小時當週最新文獻「快樂討論」
課程目標:
1.	希望能幫助同學建立良好的分子遺傳學實力，與激發學習的熱情。不管對於從事研究、研發、或參加研究所與國家考試皆有實質之助益。
2.	本課程注重分子遺傳學基礎觀念之解晰，希望能幫助同學將分子遺傳學觀念融會貫通，以致於在爾後研讀科學文獻時，具備基礎之學能，不致心生恐懼。
3.	將分子遺傳科技之最新發展，列入每週進度，使同學清楚掌握生物科技發展之脈動。
課程要求:
1.	準時上課、勤作筆記、勇於發問、認真複習、樂觀進取。
2.	注重原理之融會貫通、不要求死背強記一堆分子之縮寫、要求對分子機制 (molecular mechanisms)，必須確實掌握。
3.	自我要求具備世界一流分子遺傳學實力之積極學習態度。

課程概述: 本課程專為環境工程背景學生設計，核心在於引導學生認識生態學這門研究生物與環境間交互作用的科學。課程內容從微觀到宏觀，涵蓋生物演化與適應、族群動態（如增長與調節）、物種間的競爭與掠食，以及生態系統中的能量流動與營養循環。除了生態基礎理論，本課程特別強調人類活動對生態系的影響，包括全球氣候變遷、生物多樣性喪失、及大規模生物地球化學循環（如氮、磷、碳循環）的失調。課程將討論農業、能源、社會經濟等面向的永續解決方案，引導學生思考如何建構永續城市與復育受損的環境。
課程目標:
1. 掌握生態核心知識：深入理解生物圈、生物群系（Biomes）及不同生物分區的特徵，並掌握族群、群落與生態系的運作法則。
2. 分析人類與全球變遷：學會辨識當前的生態危機，如溫室氣體排放導致的全球暖化、海洋酸化及物種大滅絕，並理解人類過度開發對生命支撐系統的破壞。
3. 建立科學研究與問題解決能力：透過觀察自然、建立假設、設計實驗及使用數學模型，學習如何科學地診斷生態問題並規劃保育對策。
4. 探索永續發展路徑：瞭解生態系統服務（Ecosystem Services）的價值，探討城市永續發展、農業優化及能源轉型的解決方案，以期在環境工程專業中落實環境正義與永續經營。

This course aims to provide students with the fundamental principles of separation processes, focusing on membrane separation and electrochemical separation technologies, and integrating concepts of water resource recycling and sustainable management. The course combines theory with practice, introducing the operating principles, design considerations, and performance evaluation of various separation technologies. Key treatment units such as reverse osmosis (RO), membrane distillation (MD), membrane bioreactor (MBR), electrodialysis (ED), and capacitive deionization (CDI), as well as their system integration, will be discussed in detail. The course also examines their practical applications in areas including water reclamation and industrial wastewater resource recovery. Through case studies and site visits (e.g., to water reuse and industrial water treatment facilities), students will develop an integrated understanding from fundamental theory to industrial practice, and cultivate the engineering and problem-solving skills necessary for sustainable water treatment.
課程目標:
1. 建立薄膜與電化學分離技術之理論基礎與操作原理。
2. 理解離子傳輸、界面反應與能量轉換在分離過程中的角色。
3. 建立學生連結理論與產業應用之能力，培養面向實務的永續工程解決思維。

課名: 環境衛生與蟲媒傳染病
開課系所: 公共衛生學系 / 傳染病學學程 / 環境與職業健康科學研究所
課程概述:
隨著全球氣候異變，病媒生態環境受到嚴重干擾，由病媒所媒介的熱帶性疾病近來已有明顯升高的趨勢。台灣地處環熱帶圈的熱帶與亞熱帶區，氣候高溫高濕，極適合多類病媒繁殖，包括蚊、蠅、蚤、蜱、蝨和蟑螂等。由於這些疾病的傳播會造成流行而威脅人類健康，甚而威脅牲畜飼養等經濟活動。因此，本課程將完整介紹病媒之生物學、微生物特性、病原體媒介方式、疾病特徵和全球趨勢等。本課程透過指定課本和補充期刊選讀，讓同學了解蟲媒全球傳染病概況。學期中將安排專家演講、指定領域期刊選讀和課堂討論，以強化同學對國際間重要新興傳染病的發展近況的認識。
The ecology of arthropod vectors has been severely disturbed by global climate change. Cases of vector-borne tropical diseases increase significantly in recent years. Taiwan lays across tropical and subtropical region. The warm and humid environment provides ideal habitats for various disease vectors, such as mosquitoes, flies, fleas, ticks, lice, and cockroaches. The vectors not only transmit human diseases but also threaten livestock breeding and farming. This course will provide a complete introduction to vector biology, the etiological agents of diseases, the routes of transmission, disease presentations, and global trends, etc. Students will gain knowledge about the general situation of vector-borne diseases in the world via the required text, supplementary readings and resources, and lectures. Besides, special lectures will be given by invited scholars. Selected journal articles in designated fields and classroom discussions will be arranged to strengthen students' understanding of the development of important emerging infectious diseases.
課程目標:
本課程的目標希望同學認識蟲媒傳染病的研究和發展，並即時掌握最新蟲媒傳染病之研究進展和趨勢。此外，也期許同學在修習蟲媒傳染病過程中，體現流行病學學生在全球疫病傳播過程中所扮演的的使命和責任，提早發掘自身的定位。
The goal of this course is to enable students to understand the research and development of vector-borne infectious diseases, and to keep abreast of the latest research progress and trends of vector-borne infectious diseases. During the learning process, students are expected to discover their own places and reflect the mission and responsibility of an epidemiologist in outbreaks of infectious diseases. 
At the end of the course the students are expected to
1.	Explain effects of environmental factors on a population’s health (D17-7)
2.	Explain biological and genetic factors that affect a population’s health (D17-8)
3.	Explain an ecological perspective on the connections among human health, animal health and ecosystem health (e.g. One Health) (D17-12)
課程要求:
本課程為進階課程，以期刊論文為教學研讀主體，同學每週需參與課程報告、期中口頭與期末書面報告。
This course is an advanced course and will use journal articles as the primary teaching material. Students are required to participate in the class, give an oral presentation, and submit a final term paper.

課程概述: 本課程將首先講述毒理學的基本概念，包含外來化學物質在體內之吸收（Absorption）、分布（Distribution）、代謝（Metabolism）與排除（Excretion）等核心理論。接著，課程將介紹身體不同器官、系統，及常見的環境及職業暴露物在不同器官、系統中的毒性表現、作用機轉以及相關的健康影響。最後，課程將以新興毒性物質之毒理學議題與現代毒理學研究方法作為結尾，協助學生了解當前毒理學研究的發展趨勢與應用方向。
課程目標:
本課程旨在使學生瞭解毒理學的基本原理，包含外來化學物質在人體內之作用模式，並深入探討環境及職業毒性物質的在器官及系統的毒性表現及其作用機轉。透過系統性的介紹，學生將能理解不同毒性物質對各器官系統可能造成的健康影響，並培養評估環境與職業暴露毒性風險的基本能力，為後續進階研究或實務應用奠定扎實的毒理學基礎。

1.	瞭解毒理學的基本原理
2.	瞭解常見環境及職業毒性物質的毒性及機轉

課名: 健康與疾病發展起源下
開課系所: 環境與職業健康科學研究所
課程概述:
1986年英國流行病學家David J. P. Barker教授由英格蘭與威爾斯兩地因冠心病死亡個案的地理分佈差異，大膽提出「女孩及年輕婦女的營養、健康及發育不良是造成下一代心血管疾病高死亡率的起源」，此即為thrifty phenotype假說，又稱為Barker’s假說。之後陸續的研究證實胎兒與嬰幼兒時期的因素，足以影響長大成人後的缺血性心臟病、中風、慢性支氣管炎及糖尿病等疾病。因此生命歷程研究的興起，也象徵著流行病學家和臨床醫學家對於成人健康與疾病可能起源於胎兒及嬰幼兒童時期(fetal and infant origins of adult disease)之觀念的重新思維，而不只是以二十世紀中期以前看待成人慢性病主要與其生活型態關連之角度來解讀。

由於此早期環境暴露與基因因素的交互作用，對成人健康的影響研究涉及到許多不同領域的合作，包括臨床醫學、周產期醫學、營養學、流行病學、社會學、醫學人類學、生理學、發育生物學、遺傳學、經濟學、公共衛生學等，因此在許多學者的推動下於2000年成立了國際學會International Society for Developmental Origins of Health and Disease (DOHaD)，促進此方面科學知識的快速成長與交流。該學會目前每二年舉辦一次國際學術會議World Congress on Developmental Origins of Health and Disease (DOHaD)，今年第七屆將於9月18–21日於美國Portland舉辦大會。同時，該學會也於2009年委託Cambridge University Press出版國際學術期刊Journal of Developmental Origins of Health and Disease (J DOHAD)，本課程授課老師之一陳保中教授亦受邀為International Editorial Board Members之一。
課程目標:
「健康與疾病發展起源」課程內容主要以出生世代進行長期追蹤研究，進行跨領域科學合作，以瞭解健康與疾病的發展起源；現階段將以早期嬰幼兒健康與疾病議題進行探討，包括早產及其預後、子宮內與早期嬰幼兒環境暴露、兒童成長與肥胖、過敏性疾病、神經行為與語言發展、以及基因與環境交互作用；長期將擴展致成人疾病早期指標的探討，包括心血管疾病、糖尿病、慢性呼吸道疾病等；最終將研擬合適的疾病預防的早期介入方法及策略，以有效降低兒童及成人慢性疾病。這個課程自2007年春季第一次由陳保中教授及謝武勳主任共同開設，2009年秋季起李永凌助理教授亦開始共同授課。

本課程採用之主要教科書為Peter Gluckman及Mark Hanson兩位教授主編的「Development Origins of Health and Disease」全書共有37章，以流行病學的角度綜觀為起點，由The periconceptional and embryonic period的時期探討起，包括疾病機轉的研究Epigenetic mechanisms及A mitochondrial component of developmental programming等不同方向，延伸探討環境荷爾蒙的暴露，母親營養與胎兒發育與成長，涵括胎盤功能及其相關機轉，胎兒代謝的控制，脂肪的代謝，產前缺氧，胎兒下視丘-腦下垂體-腎上腺內分泌軸，周產期內分泌在兒童時期的影響，生長型態，胰臟內分泌功能，發育環境與胰島素分泌阻抗之相關變化。在代謝性症候群及肥胖症之探討本教科書亦多所著墨。至於在成人的疾病系統該書則探討心血管疾病的胚胎時期調控，並論及成人之腎功能病變電解質調節，肺功能影響因素，氣喘及相關過敏疾病，影響認知與行為的因素，神經系統疾病，肌肉骨骼系統的臨床觀點，癌症的早期發生學，生命週期與老化議題，內容相當豐富且具啟發性。
課程要求: 整體而言，「健康與疾病發展起源」課程主要以出生世代進行長期追蹤研究，進行跨領域科學合作，以瞭解健康與疾病的發展起源。我們盼望基於健康與疾病的發展起源之架構為探討基礎，搭起一座合作的平台，廣邀有興趣的學者及臨床工作同仁進行對談，並且和博碩士班的學生教學相長，碰撞出研究與學習的火花，野人獻曝能對於發育生物學的研究有一些貢獻。

課程概述: 永續發展科學是一個專注於研究人類、環境和工程系統之間相互作用的領域，旨在理解並貢獻解決方案。室內環境品質（IEQ）是指建築物環境的質量，它與居住者的健康和福祉息息相關。本課程重點在於永續發展科學、室內環境品質和健康之間的關係，並討論如何透過設計改善室內環境以提升健康水平。人口老化是已開發國家面臨的最大挑戰之一。本課程將回顧室內環境與健康狀況之間的關係，特別關注老年人的健康狀況，找出相關問題，並從健康生活的角度探討如何改善室內環境。
課程目標:
1. 辨識室內環境存在的汙染源。
2. 測量汙染源產生量。
3. 使用工程介入移除汙染源。

開課系所: 傳染病學學程 / 公共衛生學系 / 健康政策與社會研究學分學程 / 法律研究所 / 法律學系 / 流行病學與預防醫學研究所
課程概述:
本課程為「傳染病防治:倫理與法律實務」的進階課程。上學期的「傳染病防治:倫理與法律實務」以生動有趣的個案研究 (case study) 的方式培育修課同學在防疫實務工作上應用傳染病防治倫理原則與法律條文解決問題的知能 (competency)。下學期的「傳染病防治: 倫理與法律實務II
」則透過讓不同觀點交叉論辯的公聽會 (public hearing) 的方式，通案檢討我國目前在傳染病防治倫理與法律上諸多亟待社會溝通及修法的重要議題。本學期課程內容著重在培育修課同學看問題視野深度與廣度，從上學期的「司法」層次進一步提升到下學期的「立法」層次。
本學期授課內容包含兩大尚待解決的議題:
(1)	 針對 HIV感染者的歧視性法律
(2)	 對具高度傳染性疾病防疫措施執行法源上的漏洞
針對每一議題，本課程安排數週上課，課程中將邀請不同立場與觀點的校內或校外專家或公民團體代表到場演講（出席費將由本校傳染病中心核銷），讓同學實際體驗公聽會。
This course is an advanced version of “Communicable Disease Control and Prevention: Ethics and Laws” held in the first semester of year 104. Over the course of the last semester, students gained a competency for how principles of public health ethics and laws are utilized through interesting and vivid case presentations. This semester, through a series of public hearing process, students would be given the opportunity to exercise critical thinking by examining two unresolved issues (social communication and legislation) related to the ethical and legal aspects of communicable disease control. This semester's course will focus on expanding the scope and depth of students’ conceptions of legislation by building on themes of justice introduced in the first semester. The two unresolved issues for this semester will be:
(1)	Laws that discriminate against HIV-infected persons. 
(2)	Loopholes that allow for the containment of highly contagious patients.
For each issue, we will arrange a series of classes, and we will invite speakers to share differing viewpoints. Speakers will include experts from NTU and other universities, the government or community-based organizations (the compensation for speakers will be covered by the MOHW-NTU Infectious Diseases Research and Education Center). All students are welcomed to join our public hearings.
課程目標:
本課程希望能啟發同學對傳染病相關倫理和法律議題的興趣，培育修課同學下列知能（competency）
(1)	傳染病防治的立法層次思考
(2)	深入了解愛滋病毒感染者遭受體制性歧視的問題與對策
(3)	了解防治傳染病時, 個人權益與公共安全可能出現的矛盾, 及可能的立法解決途徑 (了解預防醫學相關措施及研究之人權維護及倫理議題)

The aim of this course is to stimulate an interest in ethics and legal issues associated with communicable diseases. Students who participate in the course will learn: 
(1)	about the legislative status of communicable disease control
(2)	how to reconsider and negotiate problems of systemic discrimination amongst HIV-infected persons
(3)	how to come to terms with the paradox of personal rights and public safety as it applies to impeding the spread of communicable diseases, and how to best legislation in such situations (Understand human right and ethical issues related to preventive strategies and research)

Taiwan has a fast-aging rate in the world. While encountering this important change, relevant health topics become important. The goal of this course is to let students understand the epidemiologic studies and related topics on aging and common diseases in the elderly. In general, the first half of each lecture will be given by the lecturer on the research method of geriatric epidemiology and specific topics on conditions and diseases in older adults. Students will read essential papers on geriatric topics. The latter half of the lecture is students’ group presentations and critique of a designated paper. Taken together, this course aims to explore topics related to aging and elderly diseases for public health practice.

課名: 族群健康中的基因學與醫學
開課系所: 公共衛生學系 / 健康大數據學分學程 / 流行病學與預防醫學研究所
課程概述:
本課程主旨在於介紹基因與醫學在族群健康中的重要性，近年來隨著高通量基因體研究技術發展，不同層次的基因分子被廣泛研究，內容包含單核甘酸多型性、拷貝數、甲基化以及基因表現數值等等，均在個體及族群層次上被證明是重要的影響因子。近年來世界各國的大型人體資料庫也將基因數據做為重要的收集資料，因此在公共衛生的研究上基因已是不可或缺的一部分。本課程將由不同層次的基因分子生物意義介紹起始，期待透過這些內容讓學生對於分析各式基因數據前能理解這些分子在細胞與個體上的重要性，接著會透過研究實例與分析操作讓學生接觸實際實驗測量產生之數據，以期能讓學生體會真實研究進行之狀況。課程後段則將介紹目前在醫院上可使用的基因檢測相關工具，讓學生能夠感受基因資料在實務上的重要性，以期讓生物理論與實務應用可以緊密結合。

This course aims to introduce the importance of genetics and medicine in population health. Recently, with the advancements in high-throughput genetics technologies, different genetic molecules, including single nucleotide polymorphism (SNP), copy number variation (CNV), methylation and gene expression, have been intensively studied and reported as important factors affecting individual and population health. Furthermore, many counties have included genetic data into their large-scale biobanks and thus genetics has become an essential component in public health researches. In this course, we will first introduce the functions and mechanism of different genetic molecules in order to let students have better understanding of the biological roles of these molecules. Next, we will provide research examples and computer practices to let students become more familiar with real data. Lastly, we will introduce currently available genetic testing tools in the real world to let students understand what genetics can do nowadays.
課程目標:
訓練學生了解各式基因相關分子之生物意義，接觸實驗數據以具備基本分析能力，進而能針對不同研究議題選擇合適的基因分子主題。本課程條列式學習重點如下：
1. 了解並分辨不同體學分子的差異
2. 了解並分辨設計不同體學研究時需注意的事項
3. 了解臨床場域使用體學資料時的應用方法與限制

This course aims to provide better understanding of biological meaning of different genetic molecules.  In addition, students must undergo real data analyses during the course and thus they should have the ability to choose appropriate genetic molecules for further investigations in different research topics. The bullet points for this course for learning are listed in the followings:
1. Understand and distinguish the differences of different molecules
2. Understand and distinguish the limitations of designing studies by using different molecules
3. Understand how to apply different molecules in real practice in fields and their limitations

In response to the increasing use of read world data and clinical databases, compared to health insurance databases, health databases contain more information beyond health insurance data. These databases allow for a wider range of study designs and statistical models. However, it also increasing the difficulty of data management, such as linking different dataset, missing value, and detection limit of parameter. This course, using SAS statistical software, aims to introduce and teach solutions to common issues in managing clinical databases, equipping students with the skills to independently organize and analyze these databases. The course will primarily consist of lectures and hands-on exercises, supplemented by discussions and assignments. During the first class, the semester's structure and expectations will be explained to help achieve the course's learning objectives.
課程目標:
本課程目標欲使學生及實際資料使用人員瞭解健康資料庫使用中常用的資料整理概念，熟悉使用臨床研究常用統計軟體(SAS)應用於實務中，且能透過將資料庫整理成分析用的資料集，並正確使用各種統計模式於分析中，並能完成初步的研究分析。
1.	熟悉健康數據整理的方式與了解常犯的錯誤
2.	瞭解統計方法使用時機與健康資料面臨問題之處理方式
3.	活用統計軟體並應用於實際資料整理與分析

課程概述:
This course aims to provide a thorough introduction to R programming skills and enable students with comprehensive understanding and practical experience in public health data analysis. The course is structured into two distinct sections. The first section will train the students on using R, statistical software (freely available), towards writing smart codes for accomplishing data manipulation, data-processing and statistical analysis. In section 2, the students will be provided with real health data and will be trained to conduct a step by step analyses protocol implementing the techniques that they learnt in section 1. Additionally, a theoretical introduction will be provided at the beginning of each class to ensure a wholesome understanding of the concepts underlying each days task. 
•	R-programming: importing data, data handling and manipulation, resampling strategies, statistical analysis techniques encompassing descriptive statistics, testing of hypothesis and regression. Data visualization techniques using ggplot2 and r-base plots, reading plots towards correct interpretation.  
•	Health datasets analysis: Real de-identified datasets will be provided. Alternately, students can acquire health datasets by themselves (if they want) or use their own research datasets too. The students will be trained and guided to conduct hands-on analysis in a step-by step manner to accomplish descriptive data analysis, variable selection, association analysis/survival analysis, on the provided dataset(s). The students will also be allowed to apply any bioinformatics tools for visualization techniques.
Combining R-programming, theoretical introduction along with hands-on analysis, the course equips participants with the skills to effectively analyze public health datasets and make informed, data-driven decisions in their research and practice. The course will for most part be computer based.
課程目標:
Upon completion the students will be able tosuccesfully do the following
•	Use R to conduct all kinds of data manipulation and data cleaning
•	Develop statistical thinking and apply statistics in modern public health research and practice
•	Describe a data set using descriptive statistics and graphical methods as an initial step for more advanced analysis in R software.
•	Implement suitable methods to formulate and analyze statistical associations between variables in a data set using R.
•	Interpret the results and provide potential explanations for the findings.
Skills that the student will gain: 
•	Data analysis with R
•	Linear Regression
•	Logistic regression
•	Group comparison testing
•	Survival analysis
•	Visualization of data 
•	Statistical thinking.

課程概述:
由每一位修課學生需針對特定主題選取一篇原著生物統計/健康數據拓析方法或理論型論文進行口頭報告並回答問題，其他同學則需評論與提問。 
In the course, each student is required to select an original methodology or application paper in biostatistics/health data analytics for their oral presentation. Students who are not presenting are also expected to actively participate by providing comments and asking questions on the presentations.
課程目標:
本課程藉由閱讀與討論生物統計/健康數據拓析之理論與方法相關文獻，將訓練學生成為相關專業人員，學習如何發掘及定義健康資料統計分析之研究議題，進而培養獨立解決問題的能力，增進科學表達以及學術專業寫作能力。

This course entails reading and engaging in discussions on original methodology or application papers of biostatistics and health data analytics. 課程概述:
This course is based on the book “Applied Paleontology”. Marine palaeontology has developed from a descriptive science to an analytical science used to interpret relationships between earth and life history. Applied Palaeontology adopts a holistic, integrated approach to palaeontology, highlighting its key role in the study of the evolving earth, life history and environmental processes. 

After an introduction to fossils and their classification, each of the principal marine fossil groups are discussed in detail, covering their biology, morphology, classification, palaeobiology and biostratigraphy. The latter sections focus on the applications of fossils in the interpretation of earth and life processes and environments. It concludes with case histories of how our knowledge of fossils is applied, in industry and elsewhere. Practicals will be included to identify and interpret microfossils using a microscope.

This is a valuable reference for anyone who is planning to get involved in the applications of palaeontology including earth, life and environmental science, as well as petroleum, minerals, mining and engineering applications.

1. 簡介(Introduction)

2.1 基本連續信號(Basic Continuous-Time Signals) 
2.2 基本不連續信號(Basic Discrete-Time Signals) 
2.3 系統及系統的性質(Systems and Properties of Systems) 
3. 線性非時變系統(Linear Time-Invariant Systems) 
3.1 以脈衝信號來表示所有的信號(The Representation of Signals in Terms of Impulses) 
3.2 迴旋和(The Convolution Sum) 
3.3 迴旋積(The Convolution Integral) 
4. 連續信號和系統的傅立葉分析 (Fourier Analysis for Continuous-Time Signals and Systems) 
4.1 連續線性非時變系統的複數指數函數響應(The Response of Continuous-Time LTI Systems to Complex Exponentials) 
4.2 連續週期信號及非週期信號的傅立葉轉換(Representation of Periodic and Aperiodic Signals: The Continuous-Time Fourier Series and Transform) 
4.3 迴旋特性(The Convolution Properity)4.4 調變特性(The Modulation Properity) 
4.5 線性常數係數微分方程所描述的系統的頻率響應(The Frequency Response of Systems Characterized by Linear Constant-Coefficient Differential Equations) 
4.6 一階及二階系統(First-Order and Second-Order Systems) 
5. 不連續信號和系統的傅立葉分析 (Fourier Analysis for Discrete -Time Signals and Systems) 
5.1 不連續線性非時變系統的複數指數函數響應(The Response of 
Discrete-Time LTI Systems to Complex Exponentials) 
5.2 不連續週期信號及非週期信號的傅立葉轉換(Representation of Periodic and Aperiodic Signals: The Discrete-Time Fourier Series and Transform) 
5.3 迴旋特性(The Convolution Properity) 
5.4 調變特性(The Convolution Properity) 
5.5 線性常數係數差分方程所描述的系統的頻率響應(The Frequency Response of Systems Characterized by Linear Constant-Coefficient Difference Equations) 
5.6 一階及二階系統(First-Order and Second-Order Systems) 
6. 濾波(Filtering) 
6.1 理想及非理想的頻率濾波(Ideal and Nonideal Frequency-Selective Filters) 
6.2 微分方程所描述的頻率濾波(Examples of Continuous-Time Frequency-Selective Filters Described by Differential Equations) 
6.3 差分方程所描述的頻率濾波(Examples of Discrete-Time Frequency-Selective Filters Described by Difference Equations) 
7. 調變(Modulation) 
7.1 連續正弦信號振幅調變及其應用(Continuous-Time Sinusoidal Amplitude Modulation and Its Applications) 
7.2 單邊振幅調變(Single-Sideband Amplitude Modulation) 
7.3 不連續正弦信號振幅調變(Discrete-Time Amplitude Modulation) 
7.4 連續信號頻率調變(Continuous-Time Frequency Modulation) 
8. 取樣(Sampling)
8.1 取樣理論: 以取樣值表示連續時間信號(Representation of a Continuous-Time Signal by Its Samples:
The Sampling Theorem)
8.2 利用內插法從取樣信號恢復原信號(Reconstruction of a Signal from Its Samples Using
Interpolation)
8.3 不完全取樣的影響: 膺頻效應(The Effect of Undersampling: Aliasing)
8.4 連續時間信號的離散時間處理(Discrete-Time Processing of Continuous-Time Signals)
8.5 離散時間信號取樣( Sampling of Discrete-Time Signals )

課程概述:
〔計算波浪力學〕

淺水波為一簡化波浪模型，在自然環境與人造環境中皆有許多運用，例如：海嘯、波浪於近岸的演變、颱風暴潮、河流、山崩與雪崩。

此課程為對數值方法及流體力學已有所了解的研究所新生以及大學部高年級生設計，將探討淺水波方程式之推導、運用、以及解答方法。學生將會學習如何在自己的數值模型中實現基本的有限差分法和有限體積法，透過收斂性測試和基準測試來檢查數值模型的表現，並以技術報告形式呈現成果。課堂中亦會討論線性淺水波方程式的解析解、以及近代新穎的非線性淺水波方程式之震波捕捉數值計算方法。最後，課程將導入計算流體力學CFD的基本原理。

於此課程中，學生將會大幅增進與數值計算相關的寫程式能力和科學寫作的能力。

本課程將引導學生認識嵌入式系統，並使用ARM微處理器當學習媒介。課程當中將學習ARM微處理器架構及其組合語言並介紹處理器與各式I/O之互動。本課程將搭配實驗，先使用嵌入式C語言輕易地控制各式I/O，最後介紹用課堂所學之組合語言進行控制，讓學生深入了解微處理器架構、低階機器語言、組合語言、高階程式語言如C語言相互之間的關係。

課程概述:
總體經濟除了追求經濟成長，並也同時追求物價穩定、充分就業、及減少貧富差距等目標。但在這幾項目標有所衝突時，如何取捨並排定輕重緩急，就往往是政治，而非經濟的議題。也就是說，例如是否要接受通膨率升高1%，做為降低失業率1%的代價，可能是政治上的考量；但是政策該如何制訂，以避免通膨上升了1%，失業率卻僅下降0.5%，這就是總體經濟學的範疇了。

另外，例如台灣去年(2025)經濟成長率創下7.3% 的亮麗成績，這就像整個國家一起做一塊大餅，這塊餅的份量較2024年擴大了7.3%，但參與做餅的是那些人(部門)？分到餅的又是哪些人(部門)? 如果經濟成長造成的是分配愈來愈不均衡的結果，那麼政策上該如何制定才能改善這情況？這些議題，都是本學期將討論的。
課程目標: 本課程基本上為已修過經原的同學開授，然曾修習過經原並非修課必要條件，若外系有興趣，也歡迎選修。本課程著重於「理論應用於實務問題的分析」；儘管同學對於總經理論可能已有基本瞭解，但面對財政與貨幣政策等實務問題時，可能難以與理論結合。因此，本課程希望能增進同學分析實務問題的能力。

本課程的首要目標在於讓學生全面熟悉解讀複雜財務報表所需的多面向分析技能。在此基礎目標之上，本課程旨在協助已具備充分會計基礎與財務基礎的學生，完成從單純的報表資料編製到具備洞見的資料解讀的能力。本課程所要求的先修課程已訓練同學理解基本財務理論，並熟悉記錄財務交易與理解會計原則的機制，而本課程的重點則在於理解深入分析財務報表，以及準確評估整體企業價值所不可或缺的理論概念與實務技巧。

課程目標:
在人工智慧蓬勃發展的今日，現今大學乃至於統計課程的學習環境也因此劇烈變化；而讓我們能因應這些發展與變化的一個方式，是強化自身的邏輯思考能力。
而高等統計學傳統上為統計學的進階課程，以邏輯論證與推導的方式瞭解統計概念的內涵，本課程則為「高等統計上」課程的接續(但先修課程不包括「高等統計上」)，而置重點於抽樣、點估計、區間估計、檢定、及線性迴歸等部分。
在結合上述發展與變化後，首先，本課程將課程目標轉變為：透過統計概念內涵的學習，強化自身的邏輯思考能力；第二，統計學有一特性為其在應用至各學科時，與學科之結合過程亦為同學必要之學習，此一結合過程以經濟與商管財金領域為例，關鍵字即為計量(經濟學)；第三，本課程在內容上將比傳統高統課花費更多的時間於整合(初等)統計學(、或計量導論)與高統課的思維，在難度上也將較傳統高統與數理統計學(先修課程對微積分的要求更多(至少8學分或微甲))課程低，但將能使修課同學更易於了解高統、初統、計量導論等三課程各自的定位，也得以強化對初統或計量導論的理解。
總之，本課程適合以下三類型同學：
1.想強化自身邏輯思考能力的同學、
2.想強化統計學(但不包含計量經濟學)中屬於邏輯論證與推導部分學習(但留意本課程難度較傳統高統課略低)的同學、以及
3.已修過初統或計量導論課，但想要再補強感覺的同學。(註1, 註2)

課程概述:
The course is designed for undergraduate students. This course provides a rigorous introduction to the economic and financial foundations of risk management and insurance. Designed for undergraduate students, the course aims to develop a systematic understanding of insurance theories, as well as how risk is perceived, measured, priced, and managed under uncertainty. The course combines classical economic theory with contemporary research in insurance economics, insurance finance, and risk management. 

The first part of the course focuses on insurance economics. Students study the demand for insurance under complete information, emphasizing expected utility theory, risk aversion, and optimal insurance coverage. The course then examines insurance markets under asymmetric information, addressing adverse selection, moral hazard, and equilibrium outcomes in competitive insurance settings. 

The second part of the course covers insurance finance. Key topics include premium pricing principles, actuarial foundations of insurance contracts, and asset–liability management in insurance companies. Particular attention is paid to the interaction between underwriting decisions, investment strategies, and balance sheet risk. 

The final part of the course introduces modern risk management concepts, including risk preferences, stochastic dominance, and risk indices. Through these topics, students develop analytical skills essential for evaluating and managing risk in financial and insurance markets.
課程目標:
Upon successful completion of this course, students will be able to: 

1. Understand the fundamental economic theories underlying insurance demand and optimal insurance design. 
2. Analyze insurance markets under both complete and asymmetric information settings. 
3. Explain core principles of insurance pricing and asset–liability management in insurance companies. 
4. Evaluate risk preferences using formal risk measures and indices. 
5. Apply modern risk measurement tools to compare and rank risky prospects.

課程概述:
This course is designed to equip students with a various set of analytical skills, computational tools, and research methodologies essential for producing high-quality research in Finance, Management, and Economics. It emphasizes the principles and practices required to conduct rigorous and impactful research, focusing on methods and real-world applications.
Unlike traditional courses that provide a broad overview of knowledge, this course dives deeper into selected advanced topics, prioritizing research design and practical implementation. The curriculum introduces cutting-edge methodologies, including but not limited to:
‧	Macroeconomics
‧	Continuous-time dynamic contracting problems
‧	Computational methods in economics
‧	Game theory applications in Finance
‧	Causal machine learning
‧	Regression discontinuity and kink design
A key focus of the course is on the practical application of these methodologies and the development of skills necessary for writing academic research papers. Students will receive guidance on crafting a high-quality term paper and are required to use LaTeX for their submissions.
By the end of the course, students are expected to have the tools and knowledge to conduct empirical research independently and the ability to write and present a scientific paper to a professional standard.
